items.body: ### Bug Description Using new user configurable approval flow (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/51221#issue-4723062005) shows approval controls on CLI, but not on desktop or in gateways. Tool is called, and model reports "need approval", but actual approval controls aren't visible. ### Steps to Reproduce Minimal plugin (`~/.hermes/plugins/approval-test/`), gating one read-only MCP tool: ```yaml # plugin.yaml name: approval-test version: "0.1.0" description: "test: require approval for one MCP tool" hooks: - pre_tool_call ``` ```python # __init__.py def _on_pre_tool_call(tool_name="", args=None, **_): if tool_name == "mcp__fastmail_jmap_tools__list_inbox": return {"action": "approve", "message": "test: requires approval"} return None def register(ctx): ctx.register_hook("pre_tool_call", _on_pre_tool_call) ``` Enabled via `plugins.enabled: [approval-test]` in config.yaml. - CLI (`hermes`, interactive): ask something that triggers the gated tool. The approval prompt appears in the terminal; answering `o` runs the tool. Works as designed. - Desktop app: same request. The tool call is intercepted and blocked, the model relays "approval required" to the user, but no approval dialog or notification appears anywhere in the UI. Retrying stays blocked. There is no way to approve the action from the desktop. ### Expected Behavior Approval controls should show on desktop and gateways. ### Actual Behavior Approval controls don't show on desktop and gateways. ### Affected Component Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) Telegram ### Debug Report ```shell Report https://paste.rs/Ydugw agent.log https://paste.rs/PGtF0 gateway.log https://paste.rs/xshvY gui.log https://paste.rs/q5zis desktop.log https://paste.rs/ZorZL ``` ### Operating System macOS 26.5.2 ### Python Version 3.14.6 ### Hermes Version v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) Two different gateway approval transports exist, and the plugin escalation is wired to the dead one (line refs as of 9d2ff58): - Working path (terminal / execute_code guards): `check_all_command_guards()` uses the per-session notify callback (`_gateway_notify_cbs`) and blocks in `_await_gateway_decision()` (`tools/approval.py:2297`). The callback emits `approval.request` into the gateway event stream (e.g. `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` `_approval_notify`), which the desktop approval component and the messaging `/approve`/`!approve` commands consume. - Plugin path: `resolve_pre_tool_block()` → `request_tool_approval()` (`tools/approval.py:2179`) → `_run_approval_gate()`, whose gateway branch calls `submit_pending()` and immediately returns `approved: false / status: approval_required`. `submit_pending()` (`tools/approval.py:1458`) only assigns `_pending[session_key]` — nothing ever reads that dict back out (its only other reference is the pop in `clear_session()`), no notify callback fires, and no `approval.request` event is emitted. `/approve` resolves the blocking queue via `resolve_gateway_approval`/`has_blocking_approval`, so it reports no pending approval for these. `_run_approval_gate()` was extracted from the tail of `check_dangerous_command()`, which still carried the legacy `submit_pending` branch — but the entry point actually used for commands in gateway sessions is `check_all_command_guards()`, which got the blocking transport. The plugin escalation inherited the legacy branch. ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Telegram gateway connect() hangs indefinitely on first attempt at container boot — 30s asyncio.wait_for timeout never fires

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

The Telegram platform adapter's `connect()` retry loop can hang indefinitely on the very first connection attempt during early container boot, with no error, exception, or timeout message ever logged — even though the code path is wrapped in a 30s `asyncio.wait_for` with exponential backoff that should have fired.

## Environment

- Image: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`
- Version: `Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream 19d41744`
- Image digest: `sha256:6485dfe92ab4615881f6475a85d3ec9413df8f1a6c46a6a15e6fcb19b7b8c97b`
- Runtime: Docker Compose, s6-overlay supervision (the image's default container entrypoint), host is Debian 12 (TrueNAS SCALE)
- Only messaging platform configured: Telegram (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` + `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`)

## Symptom

On every fresh container start/restart (reproduced on 3 separate clean boots), the s6-supervised `gateway-default` service logs:

```
WARNING hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs via DNS-over-HTTPS…
WARNING hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…
```

...and then hangs indefinitely. Waited 60+ seconds past this point on each of the 3 reproductions — no further output, no error, no exception, no timeout message, even with `-vv` (DEBUG) verbosity enabled via a manual reproduction of the same command. `hermes gateway status` continues to report the process as running/healthy the whole time; only an external check (calling `getUpdates` on the Bot API directly and getting a clean `200` instead of a `409 Conflict`) reveals that the bot is not actually listening.

## Why this looks like an event-loop-blocking issue, not a slow network

Looking at `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`, inside `connect()` (~line 2920 in this build), the retry loop is:

```python
_max_connect = 8
_init_timeout = _env_float("HERMES_TELEGRAM_INIT_TIMEOUT", 30.0)
for _attempt in range(_max_connect):
    try:
        logger.warning("[%s] Connecting to Telegram (attempt %d/%d)…", ...)
        await asyncio.wait_for(self._app.initialize(), timeout=_init_timeout)
        break
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        ...
        logger.warning("[%s] Connect attempt %d/%d timed out after %.0fs — retrying in %ds", ...)
        await asyncio.sleep(wait)
    except (NetworkError, TimedOut, OSError) as init_err:
        ...
```

This is well-designed — a 30s timeout with exponential backoff. But in every one of the 3 hung boots, the `"Connect attempt 1/8 timed out after 30s — retrying in Xs"` message **never appeared**, despite waiting well past 30 seconds (60+ seconds each time). If `self._app.initialize()` (python-telegram-bot's `Application.initialize()`) were merely slow due to network latency, `asyncio.wait_for` should have cancelled it at the 30s mark and logged the retry message — that never happened.

This strongly suggests something inside `self._app.initialize()` (possibly a synchronous/blocking DNS resolution or socket call at the OS level, not a cooperative `await`) is blocking the event loop itself, preventing `asyncio.wait_for`'s own timeout callback from ever getting a chance to fire.

## Why I suspect a boot-time race, not a permanent network problem

- IPv6 was ruled out: the container's IPv6 route was non-functional (confirmed via `curl -6` failing while `curl -4` succeeded in ~0.1s), and disabling IPv6 at the container level (`sysctls: net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1`) did **not** fix the hang — it was necessary for other reasons but not sufficient here.
- `--replace` and `HERMES_S6_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1` were ruled out as the cause: reproducing the **exact** command the s6 run-script uses (`HERMES_S6_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1 hermes gateway run --replace --no-supervise -vv`) manually via `docker exec`, a few seconds *after* the container had already been running, connected successfully and immediately — twice in a row, with full `getMe` → `deleteWebhook` → `setMyCommands` → polling startup completing in about 1 second.
- The only difference between the two scenarios is **when** the command runs relative to container boot: the s6-supervised invocation (via the auto-generated `/run/service/gateway-default/run` script, created by `hermes_cli.container_boot` → `S6ServiceManager._render_run_script()`) starts within the first couple of seconds of container life, before `01-hermes-setup`/`stage2-hook.sh` even fully completes some steps. A manual invocation run afterward, once the container's network/DNS is fully settled, works every time.
- I checked the full boot chain (`stage2-hook.sh`, `entrypoint.sh`, `main-wrapper.sh`, the static `s6-rc.d` service tree, `container_boot.py`) for any existing "wait for network/DNS" mechanism — there is none. Services start in a fixed sequence with no readiness gating.

## What I did NOT do

I deliberately did not patch anything inside the image. The run script that would need a startup delay (`/run/service/gateway-default/run`) is regenerated from scratch on every container boot from Python code (`S6ServiceManager._render_run_script`), so a local file edit would not survive a restart, and there's no documented environment variable or user-hook mechanism (e.g. no `custom-cont-init.d` convention) to add a delay from outside the package. Patching `adapter.py`/`service_manager.py` directly felt too fragile (lost on every image update) for what looks like it should be fixed at the source.

## Suggested areas to look at (not prescriptive — you know this code much better than I do)

- Whether `self._app.initialize()` (or something it calls — possibly the "Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs via DNS-over-HTTPS" step, or python-telegram-bot's own bootstrap/`getMe` call) performs a blocking/synchronous network or DNS call somewhere instead of a properly awaited one, which would explain why `asyncio.wait_for`'s cancellation never gets a chance to run.
- Whether the `gateway-default` s6 service could benefit from a short bounded wait for network readiness (e.g. resolving a well-known host, or checking `/etc/resolv.conf`'s nameserver is reachable) before the very first `hermes gateway run --replace` invocation at container boot, distinct from the existing per-attempt retry/backoff which is designed for later transient failures.

## Reproduction steps

1. `docker-compose.yml` with only the `hermes-agent` service (Telegram configured via `.env`, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` + `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`).
2. `docker compose up -d` (or `docker restart hermes-agent` on an existing container).
3. `docker logs -f hermes-agent | grep -i telegram` — observe it stop at `Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…` indefinitely.
4. Confirm it's not just slow to log by checking `docker exec hermes-agent curl -s https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates` — returns a clean `200 {"ok":true,"result":[...]}"` (should be `409 Conflict` if actually connected/polling).
5. Wait, then `docker exec hermes-agent hermes gateway stop && docker exec -d hermes-agent hermes gateway run --replace` — connects instantly this time.

Happy to provide the full `-vv` logs from the manual reproduction if useful, or run additional diagnostics — this is a home lab / small deployment so I have full access to poke at it further.

items.title: TUI gateway leaks the freshly built AIAgent when the session is closed mid-build
items.body:
### What happens

The TUI gateway builds a session's `AIAgent` lazily on a background thread. If the session is closed while that build is still in flight — fast `/new` churn, or a quick disconnect/reconnect — the agent that finishes building afterwards is attached to the already-reaped session and never closed. The agent, and the network clients / resources it owns, leaks until the gateway shuts down.

### Where

`tui_gateway/server.py`, `_start_agent_build` → `_build`, racing against `session.close` → `_teardown_session`.

Agent construction is expensive (tool discovery, model metadata, MCP discovery), so the race window is wide. `session.close` closes whatever it finds on the session dict at that instant: if it runs before `_build` has attached the agent, it sees `agent=None` and closes nothing. `_build` then finishes and unconditionally stores the agent on the now-dead session — and nothing ever closes it.

### Why it is reachable

The neighbouring resources are already protected against exactly this race — `_attach_worker` closes the slash worker if the session was reaped, and the `_build` `finally` block unregisters a late approval-notify callback. The freshly built agent itself is the remaining gap. (The nearby reaper work, e.g. #48656 / #41473, covers orphaned *slash_worker* subprocesses, not this in-process agent.)

### Reproduction

Drive `session.create`, block inside `_make_agent` until the build thread is parked, fire `session.close`, then release the build. On current `main` the late-built agent is never closed (`closed_agents == []`), a slash worker is spawned and a notify callback registered for the dead session.

### Expected

A session closed mid-build should close the just-built agent (and skip worker/notify setup), the same way the worker and notify paths already handle the race.

A fix with a regression test is in #49756.

items.title: Desktop sidebar creates duplicate 'main' lane for non-git project folders

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Bug

When a Hermes Project is bound to a folder that is **not a git repo** (no `.git`), the desktop app's session sidebar shows **two lanes** for the same project: one labeled with the folder name (e.g. `hermes-gbrain-operations`) and one labeled `main`, both containing the same session(s). Every new session created in that project appears in both lanes.

## Reproduction

1. `mkdir ~/Projects/test-project && echo "hello" > ~/Projects/test-project/README.md` (do NOT `git init`)
2. Create a Hermes Project bound to that folder
3. Start a new session in that project from the desktop app
4. Observe the sidebar: two lanes appear — `test-project` (backend heuristic) and `main` (overlay default) — both containing the same session

## Root Cause

Two independent systems produce lanes, and they disagree for non-git folders:

**1. Backend tree builder** (`tui_gateway/project_tree.py` → `_place` → `_place_by_heuristic`):
- When `resolve(cwd)` returns `None` (no git) and no `persisted_root`, it falls to `_place_by_heuristic()`
- This creates a lane with `label = base_name(path)` (e.g. `hermes-gbrain-operations`), `is_main=True`, `id = path`

**2. Desktop live overlay** (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-groups.ts` → `overlayRepoLanes` → `liveLaneForRepo`):
- For a session with no recorded `git_branch`, it defaults to `main`:
  ```ts
  const branch = (session.git_branch || '').trim() || DEFAULT_BRANCH_LABEL  // 'main'
  return { id: branchLaneId(repoRoot, branch), isMain: true, label: branch, ... }
  ```
- The overlay then tries to match this `main` lane against the backend's lane by:
  - `id` → **no match** (backend id = path; overlay id = `<repoRoot>::branch::main`)
  - `isMain && label` → **no match** (backend label = `hermes-gbrain-operations`; overlay label = `main`)
- No match found → **creates a duplicate lane**

## Expected Behavior

For non-git folders, the overlay should not create a branch-defaulted `main` lane. Either:
- **Skip lane creation** when the backend lane is a heuristic (non-git) lane — let the backend snapshot be the sole source, or
- **Match by path** (`repoRoot`) when the session has no `git_branch` and no `git_repo_root` — fold into the existing heuristic lane instead of creating a new branch lane

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (latest `main`)
- Linux desktop app
- Project folder without `.git`

## Workaround

`git init` the project folder. Once it's a real git repo, the resolver returns proper `repo_root`/`worktree_root`, both systems agree on lane ids, and the duplicate disappears.

items.title: cron: one-shot job executed twice when gateway and desktop schedulers run concurrently (job not claimed before dispatch)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Summary
A one-shot cron job fired twice, ~28s apart, producing two identical deliveries to Telegram. Root cause appears to be that two in-process cron schedulers were running on the same machine (the gateway process and the desktop app's `hermes serve` process), and a due job is not durably claimed/advanced before dispatch. The in-memory `_running_job_ids` guard in `cron/scheduler.py` is per-process, so it cannot prevent a second process from picking up the same due job on its own tick while the first run is still in flight.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent (git install, `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`), macOS 15.7.3 (arm64)
- Processes running simultaneously:
  - `python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace` (gateway, in-process cron ticker)
  - `python -m hermes_cli.main serve` (desktop app backend; log shows `Desktop cron scheduler started (provider=builtin, interval=60s)`)

## Repro / What happened
1. Created a one-shot cron job (ID `d9b7231ebaa4`) scheduled for 2026-07-05T21:00:00+10:00, delivery to origin (Telegram). The job's prompt involved ~2.5 minutes of web research, so the run outlived multiple 60s scheduler ticks.
2. At 21:00:31 the first scheduler picked it up; at 21:00:59 a second `Running job` line appears for the same job ID with a distinct cron session suffix.
3. Both runs completed and both delivered to Telegram (21:03:06 and 21:03:29), so the user received two near-identical messages.
4. The second run's completion logged `mark_job_run: job_id d9b7231ebaa4 not found, skipping save` because the first run had already completed and deleted the one-shot job.

## Log excerpt (agent.log)
```
2026-07-05 21:00:31,970 INFO cron.scheduler: Running job 'Reminder: <redacted>' (ID: d9b7231ebaa4)
2026-07-05 21:00:59,927 INFO cron.scheduler: Running job 'Reminder: <redacted>' (ID: d9b7231ebaa4)
... (two parallel cron sessions: cron_d9b7231ebaa4_20260705_210031 and cron_d9b7231ebaa4_20260705_210059)
2026-07-05 21:03:06,454 INFO cron.scheduler: Job 'd9b7231ebaa4': delivered to telegram:718495351 via live adapter
2026-07-05 21:03:29,640 INFO cron.scheduler: Job 'd9b7231ebaa4': delivered to telegram:718495351
2026-07-05 21:03:29,641 WARNING cron.jobs: mark_job_run: job_id d9b7231ebaa4 not found, skipping save
```
Two output files were also written under `~/.hermes/cron/output/d9b7231ebaa4/` (2026-07-05_21-03-03.md and 2026-07-05_21-03-27.md).

## Analysis
- `cron/scheduler.py` guards duplicate dispatch with a module-level `_running_job_ids` set + `_running_lock` (~line 297 and ~line 2938). This only protects within a single process.
- The `.tick.lock` file serializes ticks, but the two fires were on different ticks 28s apart, so the lock does not help once the first tick has released it.
- The job's due state (`next_run_at` / one-shot deletion) is only updated after the run completes (`mark_job_run`), so any other scheduler process ticking during a long-running job sees it as still due and dispatches a second run.

## Expected
A due job should be claimed durably (e.g. persisted "claimed/running" marker or next_run_at advanced under the file lock at dispatch time) so that concurrent scheduler processes (gateway + desktop, or any future multi-process setup) cannot double-execute it. Alternatively, gateway and desktop could negotiate so only one in-process scheduler runs per HERMES_HOME.

## Impact
Duplicate message deliveries and duplicate token spend (in this case the job did full web research twice, ~8-9 API calls each).

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop-first commits silently degrading CLI/TUI — session title lost on exit (PR #57000)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
### Bug Description

**Case 1 — CLI/TUI exit summary silently missing after `/new` + `/exit`:**

When a user starts a CLI/TUI session, sends at least one message, then exits (via `/exit` or `/quit`), the `_print_exit_summary()` function fails to produce visible output. The session IS correctly recorded in the SQLite state DB (messages, title, duration), but the terminal shows only the shell prompt — no "Resume this session" block, no "Goodbye! ⚕" message, no session title, nothing.

**Confirmed on clean upstream** (all local patches reverted) — this is a pure upstream regression, not caused by local customization.

The `_print_exit_summary()` function at `cli.py:12716` is structurally intact since March 28, but the exit flow rewrite in PR #57000 changed what runs before it. The `erase_when_done=True` prompt_toolkit flag, the `_clear_terminal_on_exit()` call, and the session-ID rotation in `_persist_active_session_before_close()` combine to make the exit summary invisible when `conversation_history` is empty (after `/new`) or when the session ID diverges.

**Case 2 — `hermes project` verb delivered without config toggle:**
Previously reported as #58588 (filed as Bug). PR #49037 shipped the `hermes project` CLI verb and all `projects.*` RPC handlers with no config-level opt-out. CLI-only users discovered a new subcommand and a `projects.db` silently injected by the update.

Both cases follow the same pattern. See "Root Cause Analysis" for the full mechanism of each.

Issue updated with assistance from Ensemble (ENSEMBLE Framework protocol on Hermes Agent). Accountable human: @Pauliehedron, Conductor.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Case 1 (exit summary invisible):**
1. Start a CLI/TUI session on v0.18 (or any version with PR #57000)
2. Send at least one message (so the session has content)
3. Type `/exit` or `/quit`
4. Observe: no exit summary appears — just the shell prompt. The session IS persisted (check `hermes sessions list` — messages and title are there).

Variation: after `/new`, the exit is even more invisible because `conversation_history` is empty and `_print_exit_summary` prints only "Goodbye! ⚕" which gets lost in the clear-screen sequence.

**Case 2 (project verb):**
1. Run `hermes update` to v0.18
2. Run `hermes --help` — `project` appears as a subcommand
3. Check `config.yaml` — no `projects` section exists, no way to disable it
4. Run `hermes project list` — a `projects.db` is created in `$HERMES_HOME/`

### Expected Behavior

**Case 1:** Exit summary shows the session title (auto-generated or user-set) alongside the resume string, duration, and message count, as it did before PR #57000.

**Case 2:** New CLI subcommands and RPC surfaces representing an opinionated project system have a configuration toggle (e.g. `projects.enabled: false`) so users with established project systems can opt out. Follows the precedent set by `checkpoints.enabled` and `agent.coding_context`.

**Both:** Changes to shared code paths that affect both desktop and CLI/TUI are tested against both surfaces before merging.

*Note: Searched existing issues (pkl-extract) before drafting — no duplicate found. PR #57000 has zero comments reporting this regression.*


### Actual Behavior

**Case 1:** The entire exit summary is invisible — no "Resume this session" block, no "Goodbye! ⚕" message, no session title, nothing. Just the shell prompt. The session IS persisted to the SQLite DB (messages, title, duration all present), but the user never sees the exit feedback.

Three factors combine:
1. `erase_when_done=True` on the prompt_toolkit app (line 14914) erases the chrome
2. `_clear_terminal_on_exit()` (line 12728) clears the screen at the top of `_print_exit_summary`
3. When `conversation_history` is empty (after `/new`), only "Goodbye! ⚕" prints — which gets lost in the clear-screen sequence
4. `_persist_active_session_before_close()` rotates `self.session_id = agent.session_id`, so when `_print_exit_summary()` queries `self._session_db.get_session_title(self.session_id)`, the title lookup targets the wrong key — even when the user set a title via `/title`

**Confirmed on clean upstream** — all local patches reverted, pure v0.18.

**Case 2:** Three delivery paths, none gated:

| Surface | Entry point | Gate? |
|---------|------------|-------|
| CLI | `hermes_cli/main.py:12946-12952` — parser registration | None |
| Desktop/TUI RPCs | `tui_gateway/server.py` — `_projects_method` decorator (12 handlers) | None |
| Desktop toolset | `tui_gateway/server.py` — `_load_enabled_toolsets()` folds `"project"` in unconditionally | None |

The model tools were gated to the `project` toolset per review — the CLI and RPC surfaces were not.


### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
hermes version
Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream a05b64d6

# Case 1 git ref: 3f2a56d1a fix(cli): reliable interrupts, bounded exit, and exit feedback (#57000)
# Case 2 git ref: ffa3d3c81 Merge pull request #49037 from NousResearch/bb/projects-paradigm
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.1

### Python Version

3.11.9

### Hermes Version

v0.18.0 (2026.7.1)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
N/A — neither case produces errors or tracebacks. Both are silent behavior changes.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)


**Case 1 — Session title missing (PR #57000, commit `3f2a56d1a`):**

PR #57000 ("reliable interrupts, bounded exit, and exit feedback", Jul 2) rewrote the CLI exit flow to add `_persist_active_session_before_close()` at `cli.py:15458`:

```python
def _persist_active_session_before_close(self):
    agent = getattr(self, "agent", None)
    ...
    try:
        agent._persist_session(messages, conversation_history)
        if getattr(agent, "session_id", None):
            self.session_id = agent.session_id  # <-- overwrites CLI session_id
    ...
```

When the agent's session_id diverges from the CLI's `self.session_id` (e.g., after `/compress` or `/branch` rotates the agent's session), the title lookup in `_print_exit_summary()` at line 12748 targets the wrong session_key — finds no title — and silently omits it.

`_print_exit_summary()` itself is at `cli.py:12716-12774`, unchanged since March 28. The function queries `self._session_db.get_session_title(self.session_id)` and only renders the `Title:` line when the result is non-None.

**Case 2 — `hermes project` un-gated (PR #49037, commit `ffa3d3c81`):**

The CLI subcommand is registered unconditionally at `hermes_cli/main.py:12946-12952`:

```python
from hermes_cli.projects_cmd import build_parser as _build_project_parser
project_parser = _build_project_parser(subparsers)
project_parser.set_defaults(func=cmd_project)
```

No config read, no gate, no opt-out. Same pattern at `tui_gateway/server.py` — the `_projects_method` decorator registers all 12 `projects.*` RPC handlers without any config check.

**The common pattern:**

| Dimension | Case 1 | Case 2 |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| Upstream PR | #57000 (`3f2a56d1a`) | #49037 (`ffa3d3c81`) |
| Broken by | Exit reliability fix that rotates session_id | Desktop projects feature without config gate |
| Detection | Human noticed exit output was missing a line | Human noticed a new CLI verb |
| CLI/TUI impact | Silent omission — title disappears, no error | Silent addition — new verb appears, no opt-in |
| Fix cost | Guard session_id assignment in persist path | Config toggle at 3 surfaces + post-update check |

The pattern: a change motivated by desktop/backend concerns silently alters the CLI/TUI experience. The change is tested against the desktop app but not the CLI/TUI code path. Neither case is caught by any existing test, review, or CI gate.

This follows the same class as two earlier silent-feature deliveries documented in #58588 (`agent.coding_context` posture in PR #43316, commit `3e74f75e4`; SOUL.md persona upgrade in PR #52246, commit `411faf08b`).


### Proposed Fix (optional)


**For Case 1 (session title):**
Guard the `self.session_id = agent.session_id` assignment in `_persist_active_session_before_close()` so it only updates when the agent's session_id genuinely differs from the CLI's. When it does differ, fall back to querying the title from the old session_id before overwriting:

```python
if getattr(agent, "session_id", None) and agent.session_id != self.session_id:
    old_title = self._session_db.get_session_title(self.session_id) if self._session_db else None
    self.session_id = agent.session_id
    # Re-apply old title to new session ID if it was the same logical session
```

**For Case 2 (project verb):**
Add a `projects.enabled` config key following the `checkpoints.enabled` pattern:

```yaml
projects:
  enabled: false   # default: true (upstream behavior preserved)
```

Three gating sites (we applied this locally — 354-line diff):
1. CLI — `hermes_cli/main.py:12946-12952`: wrap parser registration in `if cfg.get("projects", {}).get("enabled", True)`
2. RPCs — `tui_gateway/server.py` `_projects_method` decorator: reject all `projects.*` RPCs when disabled
3. Toolset — `tui_gateway/server.py` `_load_enabled_toolsets()`: exclude `project` toolset when disabled

**Process (recommended):**
Before merging a change that touches `cli.py`, `run_agent.py`, or any shared surface affecting both desktop and CLI/TUI, verify the CLI/TUI code path produces the same output as before. A manual smoke test for exit summary output and `--help` surface would have caught both cases.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: IndexError in _display_resumed_history when a resumed session contains an empty message

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes chat --resume <id>` (and `--continue`) crashes with `IndexError: list index out of range` when the resumed session contains a message whose text is empty / whitespace-only.

## Traceback

```
File ".../hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py", line 661, in _display_resumed_history
    lines.append(msg_lines[0] + "\n", style="dim")
IndexError: list index out of range
```

## Root cause

`_display_resumed_history` renders each history entry as:

```python
msg_lines = text.splitlines()
lines.append(msg_lines[0] + "\n", ...)   # crashes when text == "" -> splitlines() == []
```

This unguarded pattern appears in all three role branches — `user`, `assistant_last`, and the else/history branch (lines ~660 / 667 / 673 in v0.18.0). An empty-string message makes `text.splitlines()` return `[]`, so `msg_lines[0]` raises and the whole resume aborts.

## Repro

Resume any session that contains an empty / whitespace-only message (e.g. an assistant turn that produced no text, or a blank user message).

## Suggested fix

Guard the empty case in each of the three branches:

```python
msg_lines = text.splitlines() or [""]
```

This renders an empty message as a blank line instead of crashing.

## Note

Beyond the crash, this is a mild availability issue on the restore path: a single empty/blank message makes that session permanently un-resumable until the offending message is removed. Guarding it also hardens `--resume` against a crafted blank message.

## Environment

Hermes Agent **v0.18.0** (2026.7.1), upstream `a05b64d6`.

items.title: Kanban notifier jams permanently on one bad delivery — masks the real error and blocks all notifications

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
# Kanban notifier jams permanently on a single bad delivery — `cannot rollback - no transaction is active` masks the real error and blocks ALL notifications

## Summary
The gateway kanban notifier (`_kanban_notifier_watcher` in `gateway/run.py`) can get stuck in a permanent 5-second failure loop, logging:

```
WARNING gateway.run: kanban notifier tick failed: cannot rollback - no transaction is active
```

While in this state, **no kanban→platform notifications are delivered for any subscription** (silently — the user just never gets their job-completion DM). It only recovers when the offending subscription is manually removed (`kanban notify-unsubscribe`).

## Root cause
`write_txn()` in `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`:

```python
def write_txn(conn):
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        yield conn
    except Exception:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")   # <-- raises if the txn is already not active
        raise
    else:
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
```

When an error occurs inside the transaction body and the transaction is already no longer active, the `conn.execute("ROLLBACK")` in the `except` handler **itself raises** `cannot rollback - no transaction is active`. That secondary exception **masks the original error**, so the true failure (in `claim_unseen_events_for_sub` / event processing) is never surfaced.

Compounding it: the notifier tick appears to abort the whole cycle when one subscription throws, so a single un-deliverable event blocks delivery for every other subscription too, and it retries forever.

## Impact
- Silent, user-facing: job-completion / blocked DMs stop arriving with no error shown to the user.
- Global: one stuck subscription blocks the entire notifier, not just that task.
- Only visible in `gateway.log`.

## Reproduction (observed)
1. Create a kanban task with a Discord notify subscription.
2. Let it complete. Intermittent: the first task's completion DM delivered fine; a second, identical task's completion jammed the notifier into the loop above and never delivered.
3. `kanban notify-list <task>` shows the sub still pending at `since event 0`; `kanban notify-unsubscribe <task> ...` clears the jam and the 5s error loop stops immediately.

## Suggested fix
1. Make `write_txn`'s rollback defensive so it can't mask the primary error, e.g.:
   ```python
   except Exception:
       try:
           conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
       except Exception:
           pass
       raise
   ```
   This surfaces the real underlying exception instead of `cannot rollback ...`.
2. Isolate per-subscription failures in the notifier tick (try/except per sub) so one un-deliverable event cannot block delivery for all other subscriptions.
3. (Follow-up) The underlying primary error that this masks — likely in `claim_unseen_events_for_sub` — should be diagnosable once (1) is in, and fixed on its own.

## Environment
- NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), Ubuntu 24.04
- Hermes gateway (`hermes-gateway.service`), running against a local Nemotron model
- Python `sqlite3` for the kanban board DB

items.title: fix(qqbot): QQAdapter.connect() missing is_reconnect parameter — TypeError on reconnect

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Description

QQBot platform fails to connect/reconnect with a TypeError:

```
QQAdapter.connect() got an unexpected keyword argument 'is_reconnect'
```

The error triggers immediately on first connect and repeats every reconnect attempt with exponential backoff (60s → 120s → 240s → 300s). QQ remains permanently unavailable until the fix is applied.

## Root Cause

Commit `43b8ba418` (fix(telegram): preserve Bot API update queue on watcher reconnect) changed the abstract base class signature in `gateway/platforms/base.py:2864`:

```python
# Base class (abstractmethod)
async def connect(self, *, is_reconnect: bool = False) -> bool:
```

Every other platform adapter was updated to match — but **QQAdapter** was missed:

```python
# gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py:281
async def connect(self) -> bool:  # ← missing is_reconnect parameter
```

The gateway passes `connect(is_reconnect=True/False)` per the new interface; QQAdapter does not accept the keyword argument → TypeError → reconnect loop.

## Fix

One-line signature fix in `gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py`:

```python
# Before
async def connect(self) -> bool:

# After
async def connect(self, *, is_reconnect: bool = False) -> bool:
```

QQ already does a full fresh auth + WebSocket on every connect call, so it is safe to accept and ignore the `is_reconnect` flag — same pattern as other stateless adapters (e.g., WhatsApp, WeChat).

## Existing Related Issues

- #52914 (fishlikeX)
- #53443 (crayontomas)
- #54410 (liuyaowei) — same bug, all still open

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: any version after commit `43b8ba418`
- Platform: qqbot
- Effect: QQ channel entirely dead until patched locally

items.title: hermes update overwrites gateway/run.py, dropping hermes-feishu-streaming-card sidecar hook

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## What happened

After running `hermes update` (which bumped from v0.17.0 to v0.18.0 / v2026.7.1), the `hermes-feishu-streaming-card` sidecar stopped working. The Feishu streaming card (interactive card replies in Feishu/Lark) silently failed to start.

The root cause: `hermes update` performs a git reset/checkout that overwrites `gateway/run.py`, which removes the hook injected by `hermes-feishu-streaming-card`'s installer. The sidecar's manifest (`.hermes_feishu_card_manifest`) survives the update and still references the old SHA, but the actual hook code in `run.py` is gone.

## Root cause

`hermes-feishu-streaming-card` (v3.6.3, installed via pip as a sidecar plugin) patches two files during its `install` step:

1. `gateway/run.py` -- injects a hook to start the streaming card sidecar when the gateway boots
2. `cron/scheduler.py` -- injects a hook for card-related cron tasks

It saves backups (`run.py.hermes_feishu_card.bak`, `scheduler.py.hermes_feishu_card.bak`) and a manifest (`.hermes_feishu_card_manifest`) tracking the patched file SHAs.

When `hermes update` runs, it does a `git pull`/`git checkout` that overwrites `gateway/run.py` with the fresh upstream copy. The backup files and manifest survive, but the hook is gone. The sidecar CLI refuses to reinstall because it detects "run.py changed since install" -- it sees the file differs from its backup, but the hook is missing.

Error from `hermes-feishu-card doctor` after update:
```
error: run.py changed since install; refusing to install
```

And on gateway restart:
```
[hermes] [hermes-feishu-card] hook failed: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_feishu_card'
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (v2026.7.1)
- `hermes-feishu-streaming-card` v3.6.3 (baileyh8/hermes-feishu-streaming-card)
- macOS 15.x

## Workaround

Manually reinstall the sidecar hook:
```
hermes-feishu-card install --config ~/.hermes_feishu_card/config.yaml --hermes-dir ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
```

Or if the install command refuses due to SHA mismatch, force-restore from backup and reinstall:
```
hermes-feishu-card restore --config ~/.hermes_feishu_card/config.yaml --hermes-dir ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
hermes-feishu-card install --config ~/.hermes_feishu_card/config.yaml --hermes-dir ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
```

## Suggested fix

This is the same class of bug as #59169 (Photon sidecar npm deps not reinstalled after update). Two approaches:

1. **In `hermes-feishu-streaming-card`**: Make the sidecar auto-detect that `run.py` has been reverted and self-heal by reapplying its hook on next gateway boot, similar to PR #59213's approach for Photon.

2. **In `hermes update`**: Before doing a git checkout, save and restore any known sidecar hooks/manifests, or provide a `post-update` hook mechanism that third-party sidecars can register into.

The broader pattern: `hermes update` assumes only first-party code lives under the repo, but sidecar plugins legitimately patch a few files there. An update hook/callback mechanism would let all sidecars (Photon, Feishu card, others) reapply their patches after an update.

items.title: Gemini OpenAI-compat: extra_body.google.thinking_config double-nested (400, surfaced as generic empty response)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Bug

In `agent/transports/chat_completions.py` (around line 432-439), the Gemini OpenAI-compat
`thinking_config` builder nests the payload one level too deep:

```python
if thinking_config:
    openai_compat_extra = extra_body.get("extra_body", {})   # reads "extra_body" key from itself
    google_extra = openai_compat_extra.get("google", {})
    google_extra["thinking_config"] = thinking_config
    openai_compat_extra["google"] = google_extra
    extra_body["extra_body"] = openai_compat_extra            # double-wraps
```

`extra_body` here becomes `api_kwargs["extra_body"]`, which the OpenAI SDK merges
directly into the top-level JSON request body. Wrapping the payload in another
`"extra_body"` key produces:

```json
{"extra_body": {"extra_body": {"google": {"thinking_config": {...}}}}}
```

instead of the correct:

```json
{"extra_body": {"google": {"thinking_config": {...}}}}
```

## Impact

Google's API rejects the request with `400 Invalid JSON payload... Unknown name
"extra_body" at 'extra_body': Cannot find field.` — confirmed by replaying the exact
captured request body directly against
`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/chat/completions` via curl.

Hermes does not surface this — it retries 3x and reports a generic
`⚠️ No reply: the model returned empty content after retries...`, logged as "Empty
response (no content or reasoning) after 3 retries" in `errors.log`. This makes a
one-line, 100%-reproducible bug look like a flaky model/API issue.

Only triggered when using the Gemini OpenAI-compat base URL
(`GEMINI_BASE_URL=.../v1beta/openai`) with a model/config that sets a Gemini
`thinking_config` (e.g. `gemini-2.5-flash`).

## Fix

```python
if thinking_config:
    google_extra = extra_body.get("google", {})
    google_extra["thinking_config"] = thinking_config
    extra_body["google"] = google_extra
```

Patch attached (`gemini-extra-body-fix.patch`) — one-line-equivalent, mechanical, no
behavior change outside the buggy branch. Verified with a live repro: after applying the
fix, a `gemini-2.5-flash` request that previously failed with the empty-response error
now returns a normal successful completion (confirmed via `HERMES_DUMP_REQUESTS=1`
request dump showing the corrected single-nested `extra_body.google.thinking_config`
shape, and a real model response instead of a retry-exhausted error).

## Suggested longer-term fix

There's a second, correctly-written Gemini `extra_body` builder in
`plugins/model-providers/gemini/__init__.py`'s `build_extra_body()` that does not have
this bug. Consider consolidating the two Gemini `thinking_config` construction paths (the
newer plugin-based `build_extra_body()` and this older inline path in
`chat_completions.py`) so this class of drift can't reoccur.

items.title: Update can wipe web_dist, and --skip-build hard-fails when it's missing — auto-rebuild or ship the prebuilt dashboard UI

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
**Summary**

A Hermes update removed the built dashboard UI (`web_dist`). With the dist gone, starting the dashboard with `--skip-build` hard-fails instead of rebuilding, so the dashboard stays dead until an operator manually runs `npm run build -w web`. An update should not be able to leave the dashboard in a state that requires manual intervention to recover.

**Environment**

- Headless Linux box (no desktop session)
- Dashboard fronted over a Tailscale tailnet hostname
- Hermes version: the wipe was observed on updates through v0.17.0. On our most recent update (v0.17.0 → v0.18.0 / v2026.7.1) the dist SURVIVED — so the wipe half may already be fixed upstream. The `--skip-build` hard-fail-when-missing behavior is the core remaining ask: it turns any future wipe (or any other cause of a missing dist) into a dashboard that stays dead until manual intervention.

**Observed behavior**

- After a routine Hermes update, `web_dist` (the built dashboard frontend) was gone.
- The dashboard service, which starts with `--skip-build` (the sensible choice for a service — no surprise multi-minute npm builds on every restart), hard-failed on the missing dist.
- Result: dashboard fully down after the update, silently, until manual diagnosis + `npm run build -w web`.

**Root cause (as diagnosed)**

The update path treats `web_dist` as disposable (it gets wiped/replaced during update), but the runtime treats it as a hard prerequisite when `--skip-build` is set. The two assumptions combined mean any update that clears the dist leaves `--skip-build` deployments unbootable with no self-healing path.

**Proposed fix**

Either (preferably both):

1. **Auto-rebuild when missing**: if `web_dist` is absent (or missing `index.html`), fall back to building it once even under `--skip-build` — treat the flag as "don't rebuild an existing dist," not "refuse to produce one."
2. **Ship the prebuilt dist in the package**: include the built dashboard UI in the release artifact so an update can never leave the box without one, and `--skip-build` is always safe.

At minimum, the update process should not delete `web_dist` without regenerating it.

**Local workaround we run**

Our systemd unit self-heals a wiped dist on restart via an `ExecStartPre` guard, roughly:

```
ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c 'test -f <hermes>/web_dist/index.html || npm run build -w web'
```

This works, but every `--skip-build` service deployment needs to independently discover and hand-roll it.

items.title: Gateway systemd unit races DNS at boot — transient name-resolution failures for Telegram and HTTP MCP servers

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

At machine boot, the Hermes gateway service starts before DNS (in our case Tailscale
MagicDNS) is ready, and logs a burst of name-resolution failures — for `api.telegram.org`
and for an HTTP MCP server's hostname — before self-recovering once resolution comes up.
Low severity since it heals itself, but the generated unit could avoid the race entirely
with standard systemd ordering.

## Environment

- Headless Linux box (systemd), DNS via Tailscale MagicDNS
- Backend: Ollama, model `gpt-oss:120b`, via the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint
- Gateway platform: Telegram; plus an HTTP (remote) MCP server configured
- Secrets integration: Bitwarden Secrets Manager (context only; not implicated here)
- Hermes version: observed on v0.17.x. Our unit carries a hand-rolled drop-in, so we haven't isolated whether the currently *generated* unit already orders after `network-online.target` — if it does, feel free to close; the ask is that the ordering ships by default.

## Observed behavior

1. Box reboots; the gateway unit starts as soon as basic networking is up.
2. DNS/MagicDNS is not yet functional, so initial connections to Telegram and the HTTP MCP
   server fail with name-resolution errors, which land in the journal as error-level noise.
3. Within a short window DNS comes up and the gateway reconnects on its own; no lasting
   functional impact observed.

## Root cause (as diagnosed)

The gateway's systemd unit is not ordered after DNS readiness. `network.target` (or an
unordered start) only guarantees interface bring-up, not working name resolution — the
standard fix is ordering on `network-online.target` and `nss-lookup.target`. The gateway's
initial connect-retry window is also short enough that boot-time DNS latency produces
visible failures rather than being absorbed quietly.

## Proposed fix

Either (or both):

- Have the generated/documented systemd unit include
  `After=network-online.target nss-lookup.target` (and `Wants=network-online.target`)
  by default, so boot-time starts wait for working DNS.
- Lengthen or make configurable the gateway's initial connect-retry window so early
  resolution failures at boot are retried patiently instead of logged as errors.

## Local workaround we run

A drop-in (`wait-net.conf`) on the gateway unit:

    [Unit]
    After=network-online.target nss-lookup.target

    [Service]
    ExecStartPre=<script that waits up to 30s for api.telegram.org to resolve>

With this in place, boots are clean. Filing so the generated unit does the right thing out
of the box rather than every deployment rediscovering the same drop-in.

items.title: Tool-call-shaped JSON envelope leaks into Telegram output when a local model emits it as assistant text

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Summary

Telegram users occasionally receive a raw JSON blob as the bot's message body, e.g.:

{"action":"clarify","question":"...","choices":[...]}

instead of the expected inline-keyboard (or numbered-list fallback) rendering of a `clarify` prompt. This is not a Telegram-adapter rendering bug — it's a tool-call-fidelity gap in the local model backing the agent. The model sometimes emits a tool-call-*shaped* JSON envelope as plain assistant text (including an invented `"action"` key that no registered tool schema defines) instead of issuing a native OpenAI-style tool call. Hermes's message sanitizer only repairs malformed arguments *inside* an already-recognized `tool_calls` array, so a shape-alike JSON blob sitting in plain `content` passes through untouched and reaches the end user verbatim.

## Environment

- OS: headless Linux
- Inference backend: Ollama, model `gpt-oss:120b`
- Gateway/platform: Telegram bot gateway
- Hermes version: verified on v0.18.0 (v2026.7.1) — `agent/message_sanitization.py` still repairs only inside an existing `tool_calls` array (`_repair_tool_call_arguments`); there is no guard for tool-call-shaped envelopes in plain assistant content.
- Relevant config: `agent.tool_use_enforcement: auto`, `agent.environment_hint` (custom nudge in place)

## Observed behavior

1. User sends a message that should route to the `clarify` tool (ambiguous request needing a choice among options).
2. Instead of a native tool call, the model's assistant message *text* contains a JSON object shaped like a tool invocation: `{"action":"clarify","question":…,"choices":…}`.
3. The Telegram adapter has no native tool call to act on (there's nothing in `tool_calls`), so it falls through to rendering the assistant message as plain text.
4. The user sees raw, unrendered JSON instead of inline-keyboard buttons or a numbered-list fallback.
5. This is intermittent — most turns produce a correct native tool call; a minority produce the pseudo-tool-call-as-text pattern instead.

## Root cause (as diagnosed)

- `clarify` is implemented as a normal OpenAI function-calling tool: `tools/clarify_tool.py` → `CLARIFY_SCHEMA`, with real parameters `question` and `choices`. Nothing in the schema defines an `"action"` field.
- When the model correctly emits a native tool call, the Telegram adapter's `clarify` handler renders inline-keyboard buttons (or the numbered-list fallback) and JSON is never shown to the user.
- `gpt-oss:120b`, as a weaker local model, sometimes fails to emit the tool call in the correct channel and instead hallucinates a tool-call-*shaped* envelope directly into assistant `content` — including inventing the `"action"` key, which isn't part of any real schema. This looks like the model's internalized notion of "what a tool call looks like" leaking into free text rather than being routed through the structured tool-call mechanism.
- `agent/message_sanitization.py`'s `_repair_tool_call_arguments` only operates on JSON *already inside* a `tool_calls` array (e.g., fixing malformed argument JSON). It has no logic to detect or recover a tool-call-shaped JSON envelope sitting in plain assistant text, so there is no repair path and the raw JSON reaches Telegram unmodified.

## Proposed fix (deterministic output guard)

Extend the existing sanitizer (`agent/message_sanitization.py`) with a second, complementary guard, alongside `_repair_tool_call_arguments`:

- After generation, scan assistant `content` (not just `tool_calls`) for a JSON object/substring whose shape matches a registered tool's call signature — specifically, a dict containing keys that are a superset of a known tool's required parameters (e.g., `question` + `choices` for `clarify`), regardless of extra invented keys like `action`.
- On a match, either:
  - **Re-route**: synthesize a proper `tool_calls` entry from the recovered arguments and dispatch it through the normal tool-call path, so the Telegram adapter renders it correctly (preferred — preserves user-facing behavior), or
  - **Suppress**: strip the JSON envelope from user-visible output and fall back to a generic clarifying question, if re-routing is judged too risky to do blind.
- This is a deterministic, schema-driven structural check (matching against real registered tool schemas), not a heuristic content filter — consistent with the existing sanitizer's design intent.

## Why prompt-level mitigation is insufficient

- `agent.tool_use_enforcement` is already set to `auto`, and `gpt-oss:120b` matches the enforcement list via its `"gpt"` prefix, so the enforcement prompt injection is already active — the leak still occurs under this condition. Flipping the setting to `true` is a no-op since the prompt is already being injected.
- A targeted `agent.environment_hint` nudge (already deployed locally) reduces the frequency of the leak but does not eliminate it — this is expected, since it's a weak-local-model prompt-fidelity issue, not a missing-instruction issue. No amount of prompt tuning can guarantee 100% compliance from a smaller/weaker model on structured-output fidelity.
- This failure mode will recur for any weak or local model placed behind the gateway, not just `gpt-oss:120b` — an output-side deterministic guard fixes the class of bug once, rather than requiring prompt tuning per model.

## Local workaround we run

We currently run a targeted `agent.environment_hint` prompt nudge to reduce leak frequency. We cannot patch the installed Hermes package directly on-box: it's an editable/pip install that gets wiped on every Hermes update, so any local sanitizer patch is not durable. We are filing this upstream rather than maintaining a fork.

items.title: [Desktop] Chat tab messages leak across sessions — cross-tab content mixing

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

When using Hermes Desktop with multiple chat tabs open, messages from one chat tab appear in another unrelated tab. The conversation context gets corrupted — messages that belong to Tab A show up in Tab B (or vice versa).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop
2. Create/open two separate chat tabs (Tab A and Tab B)
3. In Tab A, discuss Topic X (e.g., "StepFun step-3.5 series")
4. In Tab B, discuss Topic Y (e.g., "Alibaba Cloud API Key 401 error")
5. Observe: Tab A suddenly shows messages that belong to Tab B (or Tab B shows Tab A's messages)
6. The message routing / session binding is broken — each tab should maintain its own isolated conversation history

## Expected Behavior

Each chat tab should maintain its own isolated conversation history. Messages sent/received in Tab A should never appear in Tab B, even when switching between tabs rapidly.

## Actual Behavior

Messages from one tab leak into another tab. The conversation context becomes mixed, breaking the continuity of both chats. This suggests a session ID misrouting or message queue pointer issue in the Desktop UI.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.2
- App: Hermes Desktop
- Model/Provider at time of report: step-3.5-flash via stepfun
- Session type: Desktop TUI (multiple chat tabs)

## Additional Context

- Suspected root cause: session/tab routing mismatch in Desktop UI, possibly message queue or database pointer not refreshed on tab switch
- Workaround attempted: restarting Hermes Desktop may temporarily fix, but issue can reappear
- Related areas to investigate: chat tab component, session manager, message dispatcher

## Checklist

- [ ] Not a duplicate — searched existing issues for cross-tab / message-routing / session-mix with no matches
- [ ] Observed on latest Hermes Desktop version

items.title: [Feature] Add keyboard shortcut for archiving sessions in Desktop app
items.body:
## Feature Description

Add a keyboard shortcut to archive the current session in the Hermes Desktop app.

## Motivation

Currently, archiving a session requires clicking the ⋮ menu on a session in the sidebar, then selecting "Archive". For users who manage many sessions, this is tedious and breaks the keyboard-driven workflow. Other session management actions like creating new sessions (`Cmd/Ctrl+N`) and switching sessions (`Ctrl+Tab`) already have shortcuts.

## Proposed Solution

Add a rebindable keyboard shortcut for archiving the current session. Suggested default:

| Action | macOS | Windows/Linux |
|--------|-------|---------------|
| Archive session | `Cmd+Shift+Backspace` | `Ctrl+Shift+Backspace` |

This follows the pattern of destructive actions using `Backspace`/`Delete` with a modifier. The shortcut should:
1. Be listed in the `KEYBIND_ACTIONS` array in `apps/desktop/src/lib/keybinds/index.ts` under the `session` category
2. Have no default binding (like `session.togglePin`) so users opt-in, OR use the suggested combo above
3. Show up in the Keyboard Shortcuts panel (`Cmd/Ctrl+/`)

## Alternatives Considered

- **No shortcut** (status quo): requires mouse interaction for every archive
- **Single-key shortcut**: too dangerous for an irreversible action; a modifier combo is safer
- **Context menu only**: current approach, but not discoverable for keyboard-focused users

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop 0.18+
- OS: Windows 11 (but this is platform-agnostic)

items.title: fix: resolve_display_context_length ignores custom_providers per-model context_length

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

`resolve_display_context_length()` accepts a `custom_providers` parameter for per-model context_length overrides (step 0b of `get_model_context_length()` resolution chain), but neither the CLI nor the gateway passes it when calling this function during model switch.

As a result, models defined only in `custom_providers` (e.g. custom model names with per-model context_length) always display **256K** in the `/model` switch message, even when the runtime correctly resolves 1M via the agent switch path.

## Observed behavior

```
✓ Model switched: Happiness
  Provider: omniroute
  Context: 256,000 tokens   ← wrong, should be 1,000,000
```

Banner display and compressor context length resolve correctly because they follow the full chain (including step 0b for custom_providers).

## Location

**`cli.py` ~line 7810**: `resolve_display_context_length()` called without `custom_providers`.

The function signature already supports it in `hermes_cli/model_switch.py`.

## Fix

Add `from hermes_cli.config import load_config` and pass `_cfg.get("custom_providers")` to `resolve_display_context_length()` in both CLI and gateway model switch handlers.

## Impact

Cosmetic only — does not affect runtime context compression or API calls. Low priority.

items.title: session_key traversal guard rejects all Google Chat sessions on load (v0.18.0)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

In v0.18.0 (2026.7.1), the CWE-22 traversal guard in `SessionEntry.from_dict` (`gateway/session.py`) validates **`session_key`** with the same strict `_is_path_unsafe()` check used for `session_id`. Because `_is_path_unsafe()` rejects **any** interior `/`, and Google Chat session keys legitimately contain `/` (Google's resource names are `spaces/<id>` and `spaces/<id>/threads/<id>`), **every Google Chat session fails to load from `state.db` on gateway start**. Conversational continuity is lost across every restart, and startup logs are flooded with warnings.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.18.0 (2026.7.1)**
- Channel: Google Chat (`@openclaw/googlechat` plugin / built-in `google_chat` platform)

## Symptom

Every gateway start emits one warning per persisted Google Chat session (159 in our deployment):

```
WARNING gateway.session: Skipping invalid session entry
'agent:main:google_chat:group:spaces/AAAAEVvy5RY:spaces/AAAAEVvy5RY/threads/hrI_46qEx6c':
Invalid session_key: potential directory traversal detected
```

It affects group, DM, **and** thread-scoped keys — anything whose `session_key` contains `spaces/...`. e.g. a plain DM key `agent:main:google_chat:dm:spaces/9Il3iSAAAAE` (a single `/`) is also rejected. The sessions are silently dropped, so cross-restart continuity for Google Chat is gone.

## Root cause

`_is_path_unsafe()` (introduced in `c8eb7cf84` "fix: V-009 security vulnerability", hardened in `4d4ba0831` "refactor(session): simplify traversal guard to a helper + logger, harden non-leading separators") returns `True` for any string containing `/`, `\`, `..`, or a drive-letter prefix.

`from_dict` then runs it against **both** fields:

```python
# Validate path-sensitive fields to prevent directory traversal (CWE-22)
for _field, _val in (("session_key", session_key), ("session_id", session_id)):
    if _is_path_unsafe(_val):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid {_field}: potential directory traversal detected"
        )
```

However, only **`session_id`** is ever used as a filesystem path — per the module's own comment, sessions are stored at `sessions_dir / f"{session_id}.json"`. `session_key` is a **logical routing key** that is namespaced with `/` by design for platform-native IDs (Google Chat `spaces/X/threads/Y`; other platforms may be affected similarly). Validating it as if it were a path is over-broad and rejects legitimate keys.

## Impact

- All Google Chat sessions dropped from `state.db` on every restart → lost conversational continuity.
- Log spam (one WARNING per session, per boot).
- `session_key` never touches the filesystem, so this is a pure false-positive — there is no traversal risk being mitigated here.

## Suggested fix

Keep the strict guard on `session_id` (the value actually used as a filename), and either:

1. **Don't path-validate `session_key` at all** (it is never used as a path), or
2. Apply a **relaxed** check to `session_key` that blocks only genuine traversal — parent-dir `..`, absolute (`/`-prefixed) paths, backslashes, and drive-letter prefixes — while allowing interior `/`.

Example (option 2):

```python
if _is_path_unsafe(session_id):
    raise ValueError("Invalid session_id: potential directory traversal detected")

_sk = session_key if isinstance(session_key, str) else ""
if (
    ".." in _sk
    or "\\" in _sk
    or _sk.startswith("/")
    or (len(_sk) >= 2 and _sk[0].isalpha() and _sk[1] == ":")
):
    raise ValueError("Invalid session_key: potential directory traversal detected")
```

The most robust long-term fix is to only ever path-validate the value used as a path (`session_id`), and to encode/hash any logical key before it is used as a path component elsewhere.

## Reproduction

1. Run a Google Chat channel on v0.18.0 and exchange a few messages (so sessions with `spaces/...` keys are persisted to `state.db`).
2. Restart the gateway.
3. Observe `Skipping invalid session entry '...google_chat:...': Invalid session_key: potential directory traversal detected` for every Google Chat session, and that those sessions no longer load.

Investigate the UI rendering logic after `/reset` is triggered, ensuring that the chat component clears its state and re-renders properly without requiring a full page reload.

items.title: Gateway leaks stdio-MCP subprocesses + FDs (pidfd/pipe) for a server that never completes `initialize` — unbounded via discovery-retry loop → EMFILE
items.body:
# Gateway leaks stdio-MCP subprocesses + FDs (pidfd/pipe) for a server that never completes `initialize` — unbounded via the discovery-retry loop → EMFILE

### Summary

A stdio MCP server that fails its **initial handshake** (e.g. emits a frame that doesn't validate as JSON-RPC 2.0) is retried by `discover_mcp_tools()` on every discovery cycle. Each attempt spawns a fresh child that is **never reaped** — it stays alive blocked on `read(stdin)` — and the gateway holds its `pidfd` + `pipe` FDs. On a long-running gateway this grows without bound until the process hits its open-file limit and every subsequent `open()`/spawn fails with `OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files` (EMFILE), taking scheduled jobs and tool calls down with it.

This looks related to but **distinct from** #11202 / PR #12430:
- #11202 (and the unmerged #12430) targeted the **reconnect** path — a server that *connected successfully* and later hit a transient error, looping in `MCPServerTask.run()`.
- This report is the **discovery** path — a server that **never connects at all**. `_discover_and_register_server()` raises at `session.initialize()`, so the server never enters `_servers`, and `discover_mcp_tools()` (idempotent "retry only the missing ones") re-attempts it every cycle. The existing orphan-tracking + post-tick sweep does **not** reap these in practice.

### Version

- `hermes-agent` 0.17.0 (Python 3.13, Linux, Docker, host-networked, long-running gateway via `hermes gateway run`).
- MCP Python SDK: `stdio_client` spawns with `start_new_session=True` (`mcp/client/stdio/__init__.py:256`), so children are session leaders in their own process group.

### Reproduction

1. Create a trivial "broken" stdio MCP server that writes a non-JSON-RPC-2.0 handshake and then blocks on stdin:

   ```python
   #!/usr/bin/env python3
   import sys, json
   # Missing "jsonrpc"/"id"/"result" — fails MCP SDK validation on the client side.
   print(json.dumps({"protocolVersion": "2024-04-04", "capabilities": {"tools": {}}}))
   sys.stdout.flush()
   for line in sys.stdin:      # never receives a valid session → blocks forever
       pass
   ```

2. Register it:

   ```yaml
   mcp_servers:
     brokenmcp:
       command: python3
       args: ["/path/to/broken_mcp.py"]
   ```

3. Start the gateway and leave it running. Observe:
   - Client log repeats, roughly every discovery cycle:
     ```
     ERROR mcp.client.stdio: Failed to parse JSONRPC message from server
     pydantic_core.ValidationError: N validation errors for JSONRPCMessage
     WARNING tools.mcp_tool: Failed to connect to MCP server 'brokenmcp' (command=python3): CancelledError
     ```
   - `pgrep -f broken_mcp.py` shows a **new** child roughly every couple of minutes, and **the old ones never exit** (their elapsed time keeps growing — all blocked on `read(stdin)`).
   - The gateway's `/proc/<pid>/fd` grows steadily — one `anon_inode:[pidfd]` and a couple of `pipe:` entries per abandoned child — until it reaches the process's `nofile` soft limit and throws EMFILE.

### Observed impact (production)

On a real deployment this accumulated ~328 `[pidfd]` + ~660 `pipe` FDs (≈ one leaked child every few minutes) over ~31 h against the default `nofile` soft limit of **1024**, at which point the gateway threw `Errno 24` on every new operation. Raising `nofile` only postpones it; the leak is unbounded.

### Where it appears to go wrong (for maintainers — candidate mechanisms, not verified internally)

The failure path *does* reach the `_run_stdio` finally block, and orphan-tracking + a post-tick sweep exist:
- spawn + tracking gate: `tools/mcp_tool.py` ~L1878 (`new_pids = _filter_mcp_children(_snapshot_child_pids() - pids_before)`), finally-block orphan marking ~L1916–1943 (`_orphan_stdio_pids.add(pid)`),
- reaper: `_kill_orphaned_mcp_children()` `tools/mcp_tool.py:4858`, called from `cron/scheduler.py:3339` (post-tick) and at shutdown (`:5000`).

Yet the children empirically survive. Candidate causes worth checking:
1. The child is spawned in its own session (`start_new_session=True`), so on the SDK's error-unwind path stdin is not closed and the child never sees EOF — it blocks on `read(stdin)` indefinitely regardless of SDK `__aexit__`.
2. The post-tick sweep only reaps PIDs that were recorded as orphans in `_run_stdio`'s finally block; if `new_pids` is empty at finally time (e.g. the snapshot/filter races the spawn, or the exception unwinds before tracking), the live child is invisible to the sweep and leaks.
3. The discovery-retry loop (`discover_mcp_tools` retrying never-connected servers) has no backoff/circuit-breaker for *connect* failures, so a permanently-broken server is respawned indefinitely rather than being quarantined after N failures.

### Suggested fixes (any combination)

- On a failed `initialize()` in the discovery path, **hard-reap the spawned child** (SIGTERM → short grace → SIGKILL on its pgid) before returning the exception, rather than depending on SDK `__aexit__` under error unwind.
- Give never-connected stdio servers a **connect circuit-breaker / backoff** (like the per-tool breaker at `_make_tool_handler`), so a permanently-broken server is quarantined after N consecutive failures instead of respawned every cycle.
- Defensively **close the child's stdin** on teardown so a child blocked on `read(stdin)` gets EOF and exits on its own.

Happy to test a patch against the repro above.

items.body:
## Feature Request

Add a **token-consumption-tracker** plugin to track LLM API token usage per request.

### Motivation

Users have no built-in way to monitor their token consumption across models and providers. This plugin fills that gap by recording every API request to a local SQLite database and providing in-session slash commands to query usage.

### Plugin Details

- **Repo**: https://github.com/nuffin/hermes-token-consumption-tracker
- **License**: MIT
- **Hooks used**: `post_api_request` (existing upstream hook)
- **Dependencies**: Python stdlib only (sqlite3, datetime, json, threading, pathlib, yaml)

### Features

- Records every `post_api_request` hook call: tokens, model, provider, cache stats, duration
- Async write queue (3s flush interval, thread-safe) — never blocks the LLM call path
- `/token list` — list saved daily reports
- `/token show [date]` — generate and display a report (default: today)
- `/token save [date]` — generate and save report to file
- `/token status` — database path, size, record count
- Standalone scripts for cron-based daily report generation (`scripts/report.py`, `scripts/query.py`)
- Configurable data directory via `observability.default.data_dir` or `observability.token-consumption-tracker.data_dir`
- Environment variable overrides: `TOKEN_CONSUMPTION_DATA_DIR`, `OBSERVABILITY_DATA_DIR`

### Configuration

```yaml
observability:
  default:
    data_dir: ~/.hermes/personal
```

All Hermes core APIs used (`post_api_request` hook, `ctx.register_command()`, `ctx.register_hook()`, `hermes_constants.get_default_hermes_root()`) exist in upstream/main — no integration-branch dependency.

### Prior Art

Analogous to the built-in `nemo_relay` and `langfuse` observability plugins, but local-only and zero external dependencies.

### Problem or Use Case

When debugging Hermes agent behavior, developers need visibility into the raw API calls being made — exact request payloads, response content, tool calls, and timing. The existing `--verbose` flag and agent logs dont capture the full request/response round-trip in a queryable form.

### Proposed Solution

Add the **llm-api-call-logger** plugin under `plugins/observability/llm-api-call-logger/`. It hooks into `pre_api_request` and `post_api_request` to capture full request/response details and stores them in a local SQLite database.
