items.body:
### Bug Description

    I am seeing a usability issue with Hermes Dashboard when resuming an existing session.                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    Context:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    • Hermes Dashboard / Chat view                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
    • Resuming an existing session from the Dashboard                                                                                                                                                                                                     
    • The same general limitation is also visible from CLI resume: the session context is restored, but the user cannot easily browse the full previous conversation visually                                                                             
    • The session history is persisted in state.db; the problem is the UI rendering / refresh behavior 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    Observed behavior:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    When I open or resume an existing session in the Dashboard, I can only see the recent visible part of the conversation. Scrolling up does not reliably give me access to the full history, the displayed transcript appears incomplete.    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    Workaround discovered:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    Changing the Dashboard theme forces a refresh of the chat view. After switching theme, the conversation display refreshes and the expected history becomes visible.                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    Why this matters:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
    This makes the Dashboard clumsy for managing multiple ongoing sessions. Users expect to be able to reopen a previous session and visually review the conversation.  This is specifically important for OSs where Hermes Desktop is not currently available, such as Mac Intel.                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Click on the sessions tab
2. Select History
3. Choose a session and select the triangle icon ("play")
4. Scroll up 
5. Only the curent page and a few lines before are available  

### Expected Behavior

   • Selecting or resuming a session in Dashboard should refresh the visible transcript automatically.                                                                                                                                                   
    • The user should not need to change theme to force the chat view to repaint.                                                                                                                                                                         
    • If full transcript browsing is intentionally separate from resume, the UI should expose a clear “View transcript” / “Open history” path.                                                                                                            
    • The Dashboard should make it clear whether it is showing:                                                                                                                                                                                           
      1. live resumed TUI state,                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
      2. recent recap only,                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
      3. or the complete stored session transcript.                              

### Actual Behavior

  • The resumed session view appears incomplete.                                                                                                                                                                                               
  • Changing theme acts as an accidental manual refresh and improves the displayed state.                   

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
version:          0.18.0 [7203898c] (2026-07-04)
os:               Darwin 24.6.0 x86_64
python:           3.11.1
openai_sdk:       2.24.0
profile:          default
hermes_home:      ~/.hermes
model:            gpt-5.5
provider:         openai-codex
terminal:         local
```

### Operating System

macOs 15.7.7

### Python Version

3.11.1

### Hermes Version

0.18.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
2026-07-06 13:11:32,732 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:52493                                                                                                                                                                       
      2026-07-06 13:11:32,734 INFO hermes_cli.web_server: pty accepted peer=127.0.0.1 mode=loopback cred=token                                                                                                                                            
      2026-07-06 13:11:32,796 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:52432 reason=client_disconnect(code=1005,reason=) messages=1 parse_errors=0 dispatch_crashes=0 send_failures=0 reaped_sessions=1 detached_sessions=0                          
      2026-07-06 13:11:33,658 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:52435 reason=client_disconnect(code=1005,reason=) messages=445 parse_errors=0 dispatch_crashes=0 send_failures=0 reaped_sessions=0 detached_sessions=1                        
      2026-07-06 13:11:34,902 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:52496                                                                                                                                                                       
      2026-07-06 13:11:42,636 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:52498                                                                                                                                                                       
      2026-07-06 13:11:42,640 INFO hermes_cli.web_server: pty accepted peer=127.0.0.1 mode=loopback cred=token                                                                                                                                            
      2026-07-06 13:11:42,647 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:52493 reason=client_disconnect(code=1005,reason=) messages=1 parse_errors=0 dispatch_crashes=0 send_failures=0 reaped_sessions=1 detached_sessions=0                          
      2026-07-06 13:11:44,826 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:52502                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    This may be relevant because the issue seems related to WebSocket / PTY lifecycle or frontend rehydration. I noticed several WebSocket reconnects / disconnects around the time the Dashboard chat view appeared stale, including one closed          
    connection with messages=445 and detached_sessions=1. Changing the theme then appears to force a UI refresh/re-render and makes the transcript display update.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

 Possible diagnosis:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
    This looks like a frontend state / repaint / cache invalidation issue. Theme switching probably causes a React remount or re-render of the terminal/chat component, which then rehydrates or redraws the transcript more correctly.                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    Related issues that may be connected:                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    • Dashboard TUI auto-refresh / jumping while reading history                                                                                                                                                                                          
    • Dashboard chat scrollback not reliably exposing earlier transcript                                                                                                                                                                                  
    • CLI resume UX showing only recap/recent tail rather than full history                                                                                                                                                                               
    • Desktop/session resume issues around stale state or historical sessions                                                                

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Suggested fix:        
   • Trigger the same effective refresh/repaint/rehydration when a session is selected or resumed, instead of only when theme changes.                                                                                                                   
    • Add an explicit refresh action if automatic refresh is expensive.                                                                                                                                                                                   
    • Longer term: provide a proper transcript viewer backed by state.db, distinct from the live TUI/PTY surface.

items.title: Bug: fallback Opus→Sonnet fails with ValidationException when history contains empty content blocks

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

When the primary model (Claude Opus 4.6 on AWS Bedrock) hits a daily token quota limit (HTTP 429), Hermes activates an automatic fallback to the secondary model (Claude Sonnet). However, the fallback itself fails immediately with a `ValidationException` because the conversation history contains messages with empty `content` blocks (`content=""`) that Opus generates when emitting only `tool_calls`. Sonnet enforces a stricter validation rule and rejects those messages. The result is a double failure: Opus is down due to quota, and Sonnet is down due to bad history — leaving the user with zero response, silently.

## Environment

- Hermes version: current (2026-07-06)
- Provider: AWS Bedrock (us-east-1, Cross-Region Inference)
- Primary model: `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1`
- Fallback model: `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`
- Platform: CLI

## Exact Error Sequence (from `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log`)

```
2026-07-06 11:08:53 INFO  agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 429 - {'message': 'Too many tokens per day, please wait before trying again.'}
2026-07-06 11:08:53 INFO  agent.chat_completion_helpers: Fallback activated: us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1 → us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 (bedrock)
2026-07-06 11:08:54 WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=ValidationException model=us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 summary=An error occurred (ValidationException) when calling the ConverseStream operation: The model returned the following errors: messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text
2026-07-06 11:08:58 WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 2/3) [same error]
2026-07-06 11:09:04 ERROR  agent.conversation_loop: API call failed after 3 retries. [same error] | msgs=47 tokens=~33,992
```

This happened **twice** in a row (two consecutive user turns), both completely silent to the user — no output, no error message displayed.

## Root Cause

Opus 4.6 generates messages where the `content` field is an empty string (`""`) or an empty list when the turn consists only of `tool_calls` with no accompanying text. These messages are valid for Opus but fail Sonnet's stricter validation: **"text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text"**.

The fallback path in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` (or equivalent) swaps the model but does **not sanitize the conversation history** before re-submitting. This means the ValidationException is deterministic — it will happen on every fallback attempt until the history is cleaned.

## Impact

- User is left with **no response and no error message** for the entire duration of Opus quota exhaustion.
- If the user does not know to run `hermes modei` manually from an external terminal, the session is permanently stuck.
- The "Primary runtime restored" log message at the start of each new turn falsely suggests Opus is available, masking the underlying 429 state.

## Expected Behavior

When activating a model fallback, Hermes should sanitize the conversation history before sending it to the fallback model. At minimum:
1. Remove or replace empty `content` string blocks with a minimal placeholder (e.g. a single space, or remove the text block entirely if the message has tool_calls).
2. Log a visible warning in the CLI so the user knows which model is active.

## Workaround

User must exit Hermes and run `hermes modei` from an external terminal to manually switch the model. This forces a system prompt rebuild that incidentally cleans the problematic history. Only then does Sonnet respond correctly.

## Session ID for Reference

`20260706_110736_6e2a17` — errors logged between 11:08 and 11:11 UTC, 2026-07-06.

items.title: gateway restart can re-trigger a previously confirmed shutdown/reboot command after host reboot

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

A previously confirmed high-risk reboot command was executed **again** after the host had already rebooted and the user later sent an unrelated follow-up message (`在嗎？` = `are you there?`).

This appears to be a **resume / replay safety gap** around interrupted gateway turns involving host-reboot side effects.

## What happened

Sequence observed on Telegram plus local session state:

1. The user asked whether a forced reboot was possible.
2. The assistant replied with a risk warning and asked for an exact confirmation phrase: `確認強制重開機` (`confirm forced reboot`).
3. The user sent `確認強制重開機`.
4. The machine rebooted.
5. After the machine came back and some time passed, the user sent `在嗎？` (`are you there?`).
6. The system executed **another** reboot command.
7. This second reboot was not explicitly requested by the user.

## Evidence

### Telegram / conversation timeline

Observed from the chat timeline and confirmed against local state:

- `18:17:13` user: `可以強制重開機嗎？` (`can you force a reboot?`)
- `18:17:23` assistant: risk explanation + request for exact confirmation phrase
- `18:17:45` user: `確認強制重開機` (`confirm forced reboot`)
- later, after the machine came back:
- `19:06:51` user: `在嗎？` (`are you there?`)
- `19:07:05` Windows recorded another reboot initiated by `shutdown.exe`
- `19:09:59` user: `為什麼你剛剛又幫我重開機？` (`why did you reboot me again just now?`)

So this was not merely a delayed completion of the first reboot; the reboot was triggered again later.

### Windows event log timeline

Locally verified:

- `2026-07-06 18:17:50` — reboot initiated by `shutdown.exe`
- system came back up
- `2026-07-06 19:07:05` — reboot initiated by `shutdown.exe` **again**
- system came back up again around `19:07:37`

### Session DB evidence

In `state.db`, the relevant Telegram session tail looked like this:

- `18:17:13` user: `可以強制重開機嗎？` (`can you force a reboot?`)
- `18:17:23` assistant: risk explanation + asks for exact confirmation text
- `18:17:45` user: `確認強制重開機` (`confirm forced reboot`)
- then **no persisted assistant reply / tool_call / tool result immediately after**
- later:
  - `19:06:51` user: `在嗎？` (`are you there?`)
  - `19:09:59` user: `為什麼你剛剛又幫我重開機？` (`why did you reboot me again just now?`)

This suggests the transcript was left in a state where the confirmed high-risk user message remained at the tail **without a persisted completion record**.

## Likely root cause

This does **not** look identical to the already-known dangling `assistant(tool_calls)` replay case.

It looks more like this variant:

1. The user confirmation (`確認強制重開機` / `confirm forced reboot`) was persisted.
2. The reboot side effect happened.
3. But before the assistant/tool execution state was fully persisted and/or the turn was marked complete, the gateway process was interrupted by the host reboot.
4. After restart, the session tail still effectively contained an **unconsumed high-risk confirmation**.
5. On the next inbound message (`在嗎？` / `are you there?`), the system/model resumed from transcript state and re-executed the prior confirmed action.

So the dangerous replay here may come from a **stale user confirmation tail**, not only from a stale assistant tool-call tail.

## Related existing fix

There is already a related fix:

- `75ed07ace` — `fix(gateway): break the restart loop at the source on session resume`

That appears to cover the case where:

- `assistant(tool_calls)` is persisted
- but corresponding `tool` results are missing
- and resume replays the unanswered tool call

However, this incident appears to be one step earlier:

- the **user confirmation** was persisted
- but the assistant/tool execution state was not fully persisted before reboot

So the existing fix may not fully cover this failure mode.

## Why this is dangerous

This replayed action was a **high-risk side-effecting command**:

- reboot
- shutdown
- and potentially other future classes: delete, uninstall, kill process, stop service, remote write, etc.

A plain-text confirmation string should not remain indefinitely replayable across host restarts.

## Proposed fixes

### Option A — one-time confirmation tokens

Instead of accepting a reusable plain string like:

`確認強制重開機` (`confirm forced reboot`)

Generate a one-time token, e.g.:

`確認強制重開機 8F3K`

Properties:

- single-use
- short expiry
- bound to one pending action only

This prevents old confirmations from being replayed later.

### Option B — consume confirmation before side effect

Before actually executing the dangerous command, persist a durable marker such as:

- confirmation consumed
- action id consumed
- pending dangerous confirmation cleared

This way, even if the host reboots mid-command, the same confirmation cannot be consumed twice.

### Option C — expiry window for dangerous confirmations

High-risk confirmations should expire quickly, e.g. after 30–60 seconds.

A reboot request confirmed 50 minutes ago should not still be implicitly valid on the next random user message.

### Option D — special resume handling for dangerous unacknowledged user tails

On startup resume / next-turn recovery:

If the last unresolved user message is a dangerous confirmation like reboot / shutdown / delete, do **not** auto-continue execution.

Instead, require a fresh confirmation such as:

> I was interrupted before confirming completion of the previous dangerous action. Please confirm again if you still want to proceed.

## Expected behavior

After a reboot / shutdown command is executed once, the system should **never** execute it again unless the user explicitly sends a **new** confirmation for a **new** action.

A later unrelated message such as `在嗎？` (`are you there?`) should not revive an old confirmed destructive command.

## Repro idea

1. Ask the assistant to perform a host reboot command.
2. The assistant asks for explicit confirmation.
3. The user sends confirmation.
4. The assistant triggers the reboot command, which interrupts the gateway before assistant/tool completion state is fully persisted.
5. After restart, send a benign message like `you there?`.
6. Observe whether the previously confirmed reboot command is re-triggered.

## Impact

- dangerous duplicate side effects
- violates user expectation for one-time confirmations
- makes host-restart operations unsafe in messaging mode
- could affect any future `confirm then execute` destructive workflow

items.title: [Bug]: Telegram polling reconnect hangs indefinitely when start_polling() blocks on exhausted connection pool — heartbeat and reconnect watcher both deadlocked

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

When both the primary Telegram API server and all fallback IPs become unreachable simultaneously, the reconnect ladder in `_handle_polling_network_error` hangs indefinitely at `await app.updater.start_polling(...)`. The call has no `asyncio.wait_for()` timeout wrapper, so when the underlying httpx connection pool is in a degraded state after `_drain_polling_connections()`, `start_polling()` blocks forever — freezing the entire 3-tier recovery system:

1. **Tier 1** (`_handle_polling_network_error`): stuck at `await app.updater.start_polling()` (line 1883) — never returns, never raises, never advances to the next retry attempt.
2. **Tier 2** (`_polling_heartbeat_loop`): the heartbeat sees `_polling_error_task` as non-done (the task is alive but wedged), so it skips recovery (`continue` at line 1989).
3. **Tier 3** (`_platform_reconnect_watcher`): never triggered because the adapter never reaches `_set_fatal_error()` — the 10-retry escalation path is stuck inside attempt 1.

The gateway process stays alive (confirmed by SIGTERM receipt with `parent_pid=1`), but no Telegram messages are received and no logs appear for hours until manual restart.

## Environment

- Hermes: v0.18.0 (`v2026.7.1`, commit `5445e42b8`)
- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (Mac mini M4, launchd-managed gateway)
- Python: 3.11.15
- python-telegram-bot: 22.x
- Telegram: polling mode, fallback IP `149.154.166.110`

## Observed Behavior

```
2026-07-06 13:09:38 WARNING [Telegram] Primary api.telegram.org connection failed; trying fallback IPs 149.154.166.110
2026-07-06 13:09:38 WARNING [Telegram] Primary api.telegram.org path unreachable; using sticky fallback IP 149.154.166.110
2026-07-06 13:50:33 WARNING [Telegram] Sticky fallback IP 149.154.166.110 failed; resetting to primary DNS path
2026-07-06 13:50:33 WARNING [Telegram] Fallback IP 149.154.166.110 failed:

[NO LOGS FOR ~7 HOURS — gateway process alive but silent]

2026-07-06 20:52:19 INFO gateway.run: Received SIGTERM — initiating shutdown  ← manual restart
2026-07-06 20:52:37 INFO gateway.run: Starting Hermes Gateway...
2026-07-06 20:52:38 INFO [Telegram] Connected to Telegram (polling mode)  ← recovered
```

Notable absences in the log (expected if recovery were functioning):
- No `Telegram network error (attempt 1/10), reconnecting in 5s` — the 10-retry ladder never started logging.
- No `Telegram polling resumed after network error` or `Telegram polling reconnect failed` — no ladder progression.
- No `Reconnecting telegram (attempt N)...` — the reconnect watcher was never triggered.
- No housekeeping logs (60s interval) for 7 hours — the entire event loop was blocked.

## Root Cause

### `start_polling()` has no timeout

In `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` line 1883:

```python
await app.updater.start_polling(
    allowed_updates=Update.ALL_TYPES,
    drop_pending_updates=False,
    error_callback=self._polling_error_callback_ref,
)
```

`start_polling()` internally calls `httpx.AsyncClient.send()` which inherits the client's default timeout (typically 30s). However, after `_drain_polling_connections()` resets the polling request pool (line 1878), the re-initialized `BaseRequest` may hold a stale httpx connection that neither connects nor times out within PTB's internal flow — particularly when both primary and fallback Telegram endpoints are unreachable.

The result: `start_polling()` awaits indefinitely, the coroutine never yields back to `_handle_polling_network_error`, and the 10-retry ladder stalls at attempt 1.

### Heartbeat loop cannot intervene

The `_polling_heartbeat_loop` (line 1932) correctly probes every 90s, but its recovery path checks:

```python
if self._polling_error_task and not self._polling_error_task.done():
    continue   # reconnect already in progress
```

Since `_polling_error_task` is the wedged `_handle_polling_network_error` coroutine (alive but stuck on `start_polling()`), it's never `.done()`, so the heartbeat skips recovery indefinitely.

### Reconnect watcher never triggered

The `_platform_reconnect_watcher` (line 7560 in `gateway/run.py`) only activates when an adapter is added to `_failed_platforms`, which requires `_set_fatal_error()` to fire, which requires the 10-retry ladder to exhaust — which is stuck at attempt 1.

## Difference from #18086

Issue #18086 (closed by PR #18751) addressed the case where `start_polling()` **returns successfully** but the polling consumer is silently wedged. The fix added `_verify_polling_after_reconnect()` as a post-reconnect probe.

This issue is different: `start_polling()` **never returns at all**. The post-reconnect probe (`_verify_polling_after_reconnect`) is scheduled after the `await app.updater.start_polling()` call (line 1912), so it's never reached. The probe is a 60-second delayed task, but it's created inside the same coroutine that's blocked on `start_polling()` — it never gets scheduled.

## Suggested Fix

Wrap `start_polling()` in `asyncio.wait_for()` with an explicit timeout, so a hung call raises `asyncio.TimeoutError` and feeds back into the existing retry ladder:

```python
try:
    await asyncio.wait_for(
        app.updater.start_polling(
            allowed_updates=Update.ALL_TYPES,
            drop_pending_updates=False,
            error_callback=self._polling_error_callback_ref,
        ),
        timeout=30,  # or configurable via env/config
    )
except asyncio.TimeoutError:
    raise RuntimeError("start_polling() timed out — connection pool may be wedged")
```

This would unblock:
- The 10-retry ladder → advances to attempt 2, 3, ... → eventually reaches `_set_fatal_error(retryable=True)`
- The heartbeat loop → sees `_polling_error_task.done() == True` after the timeout → can trigger its own recovery
- The reconnect watcher → gets the adapter in `_failed_platforms` → background reconnection with 30s→300s backoff

A secondary consideration: the heartbeat loop's `if self._polling_error_task and not self._polling_error_task.done(): continue` guard (line 1988-1989) could benefit from a max-duration check — if the task has been non-done for longer than `MAX_NETWORK_RETRIES * MAX_DELAY` (the theoretical worst-case ladder duration), force a new recovery attempt regardless.

## Workaround

Manual `hermes gateway restart` from a separate shell. No self-recovery is possible once the wedge occurs.

## Related Issues

- #18086 — Telegram Updater goes silent after network blip (closed by #18751) — addressed `start_polling()` returning with wedged consumer, not `start_polling()` never returning.
- #49526 — Tailscale MagicDNS causes permanent silence after DNS failure — same symptom (process alive, no logs, no recovery), different root cause (DNS resolver caching).
- #5729 — Telegram resolver failure caching — cold-boot DNS retry budget, not runtime connection pool exhaustion.

items.title: [Feature Request] TTS voice should be interruptible when user speaks / presses a key
items.body:
## Problem

When Hermes Desktop plays a TTS (text-to-speech) voice message, the user cannot interrupt it. The audio plays to completion before the user can respond or correct. This is unlike competitors (Doubao/豆包, XiaoAi, etc.) where speaking or pressing a key immediately stops the current speech.

## Expected Behavior

1. **VAD (Voice Activity Detection) interrupt**: When the user speaks while TTS is playing, the audio should stop immediately
2. **Keyboard shortcut**: At minimum, a configurable key (e.g., Escape or Enter) should stop the current TTS playback
3. **UI button**: A stop/close button on the TTS playback UI

## Why This Matters

- User experience: long TTS responses force the user to wait before they can respond
- Interactivity: the current behavior makes voice mode feel one-way rather than conversational
- Competitiveness: Doubao and similar products already support voice interruption

## Suggested Implementation

- **Desktop app layer**: Add VAD detection to the TTS player component. When speech is detected from the user's microphone, stop playback immediately.
- **Alternative**: Add a visual stop button and keyboard shortcut (Escape) to stop current TTS
- **Config**: Expose `tts.interruptible: true|false` in config.yaml so users can toggle

## Environment
- Hermes Desktop v0.18.0
- Windows 10

items.title: 🐛 WeChat (weixin) adapter uses os.getenv() instead of get_secret() — credential collision in multiplex mode

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
## Bug Report: WeChat adapter uses `os.getenv()` instead of `get_secret()` — credential leakage in multiplex mode

### Summary

The `WeixinAdapter` in `gateway/platforms/weixin.py` resolves its bot token via `os.getenv("WEIXIN_TOKEN")` after exhausting config-file sources (`config.token`, `config.extra["token"]`). Every other platform adapter (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, Matrix, Mattermost) reads credentials through the profile-scoped `get_secret()` API. In a single-gateway multiplex deployment this means:

- **Named profiles cannot isolate their WeChat tokens via `.env`** (their only isolation mechanism).  
- Two profiles that each set `WEIXIN_TOKEN` in their own `.env` silently collide on whichever value happens to be in `os.environ` when the `__init__` runs.  
- The adapter's built-in token-fingerprint conflict detector rejects the second profile at startup — but the *root cause* is that the token was never read from the profile scope in the first place.

### Environment

- **Version**: `v0.17.0+` (main branch, commit `5445e42b`)
- **Platform**: all

### Root Cause

`gateway/platforms/weixin.py`, `WeixinAdapter.__init__`:

```python
self._token = str(
    config.token                  # 1st: config.yaml
    or extra.get("token")         # 2nd: config.yaml extra
    or os.getenv("WEIXIN_TOKEN")  # 3rd: os.environ  ← should be get_secret()
).strip()
```

Contrast with (e.g.) `gateway/platforms/signal.py`, `SignalAdapter.__init__`:

```python
from agent.secret_scope import get_secret
...
self._token = get_secret("SIGNAL_ACCOUNT") or os.getenv("SIGNAL_ACCOUNT", "")
```

`set_secret_scope(build_profile_secret_scope(profile_home))` (called inside `_profile_runtime_scope`) installs a per-contextvar mapping so `get_secret("WEIXIN_TOKEN")` returns **that profile's** `.env` value. `os.getenv()` bypasses this entirely and always returns the value from the process-global `os.environ` — which in a multiplexer is an unspecified mix of whatever was last `os.environ`-loaded.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Create a multiplex gateway with two profiles, each with a different WeChat bot:

```bash
hermes profile create coder --clone
```

`~/.hermes/.env`:
```
WEIXIN_TOKEN=AAAA-default-token
```

`~/.hermes/profiles/coder/.env`:
```
WEIXIN_TOKEN=BBBB-coder-token
```

`~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
```yaml
gateway:
  multiplex_profiles: true
platforms:
  weixin:
    enabled: true
    # no `token:` set here, relying on .env
```

`~/.hermes/profiles/coder/config.yaml`:
```yaml
platforms:
  weixin:
    enabled: true
    # no `token:` set here, relying on .env
```

2. Start the gateway:
```bash
hermes gateway run
```

### Observed Behavior

**Case A — silently wrong (typical):**  
Default profile's `os.environ["WEIXIN_TOKEN"]` (loaded at process start from `~/.hermes/.env`) is already in the process-global env when the coder profile's adapter is constructed inside `_profile_runtime_scope`. `os.getenv("WEIXIN_TOKEN")` returns `"AAAA-default-token"` for **both** profiles. The coder profile ends up polling the default profile's bot.

**Case B — explicit rejection:**  
If the fingerprint conflict detector happens to see two adapters with the same underlying token (because both resolved to the same `os.environ` value), the second profile is refused at startup with:

```
Profile 'coder' and 'default' both configure weixin with the same credential —
refusing to start the duplicate.
```

This is *a* safety net but it masks the real bug: the coder profile was never *meant* to use the default profile's token.

### Expected Behavior

`WeixinAdapter` should read `WEIXIN_TOKEN` via `get_secret("WEIXIN_TOKEN")` so that, inside `_profile_runtime_scope(profile_home)`, it resolves to `<profile_home>/.env`'s value — exactly like Telegram/Discord/Slack/Signal adapters do. Each profile then gets its own WeChat bot token with zero collision.

### Proposed Fix

File: `gateway/platforms/weixin.py`

Add the import:
```python
from agent.secret_scope import get_secret
```

Change the token resolution in `WeixinAdapter.__init__`:

```python
self._token = str(
    config.token
    or extra.get("token")
    or get_secret("WEIXIN_TOKEN")   # ← profile-scoped in multiplex, os.environ-equivalent in single-profile
    or os.getenv("WEIXIN_TOKEN", "")
).strip()
```

`get_secret()` already falls back to `os.environ` when `_MULTIPLEX_ACTIVE` is `False` (single-profile mode), so existing single-profile deployments are unaffected.

### Workaround

Hard-code the token per-profile in `config.yaml`:

```yaml
# ~/.hermes/profiles/coder/config.yaml
platforms:
  weixin:
    token: "BBBB-coder-token"     # ← must not rely on .env
```

This is fragile (token lives in plain text in config.yaml rather than `.env`), defeats the purpose of the `.env` layer, and prevents credential-rotation via `WEIXIN_TOKEN_FILE` / secret managers.

### Files Affected

| File | Issue |
|------|-------|
| `gateway/platforms/weixin.py:1163` | `os.getenv("WEIXIN_TOKEN")` → `get_secret("WEIXIN_TOKEN")` |
| `gateway/platforms/weixin.py:1162` | Same for `WEIXIN_ACCOUNT_ID` |
| `gateway/platforms/weixin.py:1164` | Same for `WEIXIN_BASE_URL` |

### Related

- `_profile_runtime_scope()` — `gateway/run.py:1372` — installs profile secret scope via `set_secret_scope`.
- `agent/secret_scope.py` — fail-closed `get_secret()` API.
- `profiles_to_serve()` — `hermes_cli/profiles.py:…` — enumerates profiles whose `.env` should be scoped per-turn.

---

I'm happy to submit the fix as a PR if maintainers agree with the diagnosis.

items.title: feat(moa): Add enable/disable toggle for individual reference models
items.body:
## Feature Description

Add a toggle switch (enable/disable) to each reference model in the Mixture of Agents (MoA) configuration UI, allowing users to temporarily exclude a reference from the aggregation without deleting and re-adding it.

## Motivation

Currently, each reference model in a MoA preset can only be added or permanently removed. There is no way to temporarily disable a reference while keeping its configuration intact.

This is a common need because:

1. **Cost control** - Users may want to reduce token usage during casual conversations by temporarily disabling an expensive reference model, then re-enabling it for important queries.
2. **Speed optimization** - Fewer reference models means faster responses. Temporarily disabling one can speed up interactions without losing the setup.
3. **Troubleshooting** - If one reference model is producing low-quality or conflicting answers, disabling it temporarily helps isolate the issue.
4. **Convenience** - Removing and re-adding a reference (with the correct provider + model selection) is tedious and error-prone compared to a simple toggle.

## Proposed Solution

Add a toggle switch next to each reference model section in the MoA GUI:

- Toggle ON (default): Reference participates in the aggregation as usual.
- Toggle OFF: Reference is preserved in the config but skipped during inference - no API call is made, no tokens are consumed.
- The aggregator should see only enabled references when building its synthesis prompt.
- Disabled references could be visually indicated (e.g., greyed out text, dimmed section).

## Alternatives Considered

- Remove and re-add: Works but tedious - user must remember the exact provider/model and reconfigure it each time.
- Separate presets: Could create a lite preset with fewer references, but this multiplies presets and does not scale well.
- Per-message override: Too complex for the UI and hard to discover.

## Additional Context

This feature would make MoA much more practical for daily use, especially for users who configure 3-5 references but do not always need all of them active. A simple toggle is the most intuitive UX pattern for this.

items.title: bug(moa): enabled toggle documented but missing from Desktop GUI

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Description

The MoA documentation states that `enabled: false` on a preset is:

> the per-preset off switch surfaced in the dashboard and desktop settings

However, the Desktop GUI (`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/model-settings.tsx`, lines 842-1078) does **not** render any toggle, checkbox, or switch for the `enabled` field. The MoA preset section only contains:

- Preset selector dropdown
- Set default / Delete / Add preset controls
- Reference model list (provider + model dropdowns, Remove button, Add reference model)
- Aggregator (provider + model dropdowns)

No `enabled` toggle is present.

## Evidence

1. **Data model has the field** — `types/hermes.ts` line 866 defines `enabled: boolean` inside the preset record of `MoaConfigResponse`.
2. **GUI does not render it** — scanning `model-settings.tsx` for `enabled` in the MoA section yields zero results. The imported `Switch` component is used elsewhere in the file but not in the MoA block.
3. **Config supports it** — `config.yaml` accepts `enabled: false` and the backend respects it.

## Steps to Verify

1. Open Desktop app -> Settings -> Model -> Mixture of Agents
2. Observe the preset configuration section
3. There is no toggle to enable/disable the preset
4. The only way to disable a preset is to manually edit config.yaml:

```yaml
moa:
  presets:
    default:
      enabled: false
```

## Expected Behavior

A toggle switch should be rendered next to each preset to allow enabling/disabling without editing config files manually.

## Suggested Fix

Add a `Switch` component (already imported in the file) to the MoA preset header row. Something like:

```tsx
<Switch
  checked={currentMoaPreset.enabled !== false}
  onCheckedChange={checked =>
    updateMoaPreset(prev => ({ ...prev, enabled: checked }))
  }
  disabled={applying}
/>
```

This would make the GUI consistent with the documented behavior.

items.title: computer-use reports unverified CUA keyboard actions as success
items.body:
## Summary

`computer_use` can report CUA keyboard actions as successful even when `cua-driver` returns `structuredContent.verified: false`. The wrapper also drops the active `window_id` for bare `type_text`/key actions after `capture()` has already resolved a target window, so keyboard dispatch can lose the same window-local targeting used by other actions.

Draft fix: #59730

Suggested labels: `type/bug`, `comp/tools`, `tool/mcp`, `P2`, `sweeper:blast-contained`

## Repro

From a clean checkout with the Hermes dev dependencies available:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git
cd hermes-agent
git checkout 7426c09bee
python - <<'PY'
import json
from tools.computer_use.cua_backend import CuaDriverBackend

class FakeSession:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []
    def call_tool(self, name, args, timeout=30.0):
        self.calls.append((name, dict(args)))
        return {
            "data": "Sent (unverified) 5 char(s).",
            "images": [],
            "image_mime_types": [],
            "structuredContent": {
                "verified": False,
                "effect": "unverifiable",
                "path": "key_events",
            },
            "isError": False,
        }
    def supports_capability(self, capability, tool=None):
        return False

backend = CuaDriverBackend()
fake = FakeSession()
backend._session = fake
backend._active_pid = 123
backend._active_window_id = 456
backend._session_id = "hermes-repro-fake"

res = backend.type_text("hello")
out = {
    "type_text": {
        "result_ok": res.ok,
        "result_meta": res.meta,
        "call_args": fake.calls[-1][1],
    }
}
res = backend.key("cmd+a")
out["hotkey"] = {
    "result_ok": res.ok,
    "result_meta": res.meta,
    "call_args": fake.calls[-1][1],
}
print(json.dumps(out, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
PY
```

Observed output on `origin/main` at `7426c09bee`:

```json
{
  "hotkey": {
    "call_args": {
      "keys": [
        "cmd",
        "a"
      ],
      "pid": 123,
      "session": "hermes-repro-fake"
    },
    "result_meta": {},
    "result_ok": true
  },
  "type_text": {
    "call_args": {
      "pid": 123,
      "session": "hermes-repro-fake",
      "text": "hello"
    },
    "result_meta": {},
    "result_ok": true
  }
}
```

Debug report: not applicable; reproduced with isolated synthetic repro.

## Expected

When `cua-driver` reports `structuredContent.verified: false`, Hermes should surface the action as failed (`ActionResult.ok == False`) and preserve the structured payload in `ActionResult.meta` so the model/user can see the driver reason.

When Hermes has an active `window_id` from a prior capture, keyboard actions should include it just as element actions and `set_value` do.

## Actual

`CuaDriverBackend._action()` only checks `isError`, so a driver response with `isError: false` and `structuredContent.verified: false` becomes `ActionResult(ok=True)`. If `data` is a string, the structured verification payload is also omitted from `meta`.

`type_text()`, `press_key`, and `hotkey` currently send `pid` but not the active `window_id`.

## Root Cause

In `tools/computer_use/cua_backend.py`, `_action()` derives success from `not out["isError"]` and only copies `data` into `meta` when `data` is a dict. It ignores `structuredContent` for action verification.

The keyboard paths build calls with `{"pid": pid, ...}` even though `capture()` stores both `_active_pid` and `_active_window_id` for the target window.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on current `origin/main` at `7426c09bee` with the script above.
- Draft PR #59730 changes the same repro to return `result_ok: false`, preserves `verified:false`/`effect`/`path`, and includes `window_id: 456` for `type_text` and `hotkey`.
- Focused validation on the patched branch:

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_computer_use.py tests/tools/test_computer_use_null_pid_windows.py tests/computer_use/test_doctor.py tests/computer_use/test_cua_spawn_env_sanitization.py -q
# 202 tests passed, 0 failed

python -m ruff check tools/computer_use/cua_backend.py tests/tools/test_computer_use.py tests/tools/test_computer_use_null_pid_windows.py tests/computer_use/test_doctor.py tests/computer_use/test_cua_spawn_env_sanitization.py
# All checks passed!

git diff --check
# passed

python -m py_compile tools/computer_use/cua_backend.py tests/tools/test_computer_use.py
# passed
```

## Proposed Fix

- Merge `structuredContent` into `ActionResult.meta` for CUA actions.
- Treat `structuredContent.verified is False` as a failed action.
- Include the active `window_id` on `type_text`, `press_key`, and `hotkey` when available.
- Add regression tests for unverified action handling and keyboard `window_id` propagation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The repro above returns `result_ok: false` when `verified:false` is present.
- The repro preserves the structured verification payload in `meta`.
- `type_text`, `press_key`, and `hotkey` include active `window_id` when one is known.
- Focused computer-use tests continue to pass.

items.title: feat: Only show configured providers in model picker, or add hide/disable option

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

The model picker (Desktop GUI, TUI, CLI `hermes model`, Dashboard) displays **all** canonical providers regardless of whether the user has configured credentials for them. This clutters the picker with providers the user has never set up and does not intend to use.

For example, after a fresh Hermes v0.18.0 install, the model picker shows GitHub Copilot, NVIDIA NIM, AWS Bedrock, Azure Foundry, and 20+ other providers even when the user only has OpenRouter and Xiaomi configured. The Copilot provider is especially confusing because its models are fetched from a public endpoint (`api.githubcopilot.com/models`) and appear automatically without any user action.

## Motivation

1. **Clarity** — Users should see only the providers they have actually set up. Showing 25+ providers when 3 are configured creates noise and confusion.
2. **Discoverability paradox** — When everything is shown, nothing stands out. Important configured providers get buried among irrelevant ones.
3. **False impression** — New users may think all listed providers are available/working, only to get 401 errors when selecting an unconfigured one.
4. **No escape hatch** — There is currently no way to hide a provider from the picker (no config option, no GUI toggle, no CLI command).

## Proposed Solution

Two complementary approaches (implement either or both):

### Option A: Auto-hide unconfigured providers (default behavior)

Only show providers where at least one credential is resolved:
- API key found in .env, credential pool, or environment
- OAuth token available
- External process available (e.g. copilot-acp)

Providers with no credentials are hidden by default. Add a config option to override:

```yaml
model:
  show_all_providers: true   # show everything (current behavior)
  # or
  show_all_providers: false  # only configured providers (new default)
```

### Option B: Per-provider hide list

Add a `hidden_providers` config option:

```yaml
model:
  hidden_providers:
    - copilot
    - copilot-acp
    - bedrock
    - azure-foundry
```

Hidden providers are excluded from the model picker, `/model` tab completion, and the Dashboard model selector.

### Option C: GUI toggle in settings

In the Desktop settings and Dashboard, add a visibility toggle (eye icon) next to each provider in the provider list. Hidden providers are persisted to `config.yaml` under `model.hidden_providers`.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Current behavior (show all)**: Works for power users who browse, but confusing for users who just want their configured models.
- **Remove providers from CANONICAL_PROVIDERS**: Too aggressive — would break the setup wizard and `hermes model` discoverability for new users who want to explore.

## Additional Context

This is a common pattern in similar tools (VS Code only shows configured debug configs, Docker Desktop only shows registries you have logged into, etc.). The credential check is already implemented in `resolve_api_key_provider_credentials()` — it just needs to be wired into the model picker filtering.

Related: the Copilot provider fetches its model list from a public unauthenticated endpoint (`api.githubcopilot.com/models`), so its models always appear even without any GitHub token configured. This makes it the most prominent example of the problem.

items.title: Multiplex: Slack adapter reads SLACK_APP_TOKEN from process env — all profiles connect Socket Mode to the default profile's Slack app

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
# Multiplex: Slack adapter reads SLACK_APP_TOKEN from process env — all profiles connect Socket Mode to the default profile's Slack app

## Summary

Under `multiplex_profiles: true`, every profile's Slack adapter opens its Socket Mode connection using the **default profile's** `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`, because the adapter reads the app-level token from process env instead of the profile-scoped secret store. Result: the default profile's Slack app accumulates N websocket connections, the other profiles' Slack apps have **zero** connections, and every message sent to a secondary profile's bot is silently lost (no error anywhere — sockets report "connected").

## Environment

- hermes-agent @ accd67205 (2026-07)
- macOS, single gateway process, `multiplex_profiles: true`, 5 profiles (default + 4)
- Each profile has its own Slack app; per-profile `.env` holds its own `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` + `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`

## Reproduction

1. Create 2 Slack apps (A = default, B = secondary profile), Socket Mode + `message.im` event subscriptions on both.
2. Put each app's `xoxb`/`xapp` tokens in the respective profile's `.env`.
3. Start the gateway with `multiplex_profiles: true`. Logs show both profiles "Socket Mode connected", and `auth.test` identities are correct per profile (bot tokens ARE profile-scoped).
4. DM app B's bot. The message is stored in the DM (visible via `conversations.history`) but **no event ever reaches the gateway** — no `inbound message` log, no unauthorized warning, nothing.
5. Independent check: connect a bare `slack_sdk` SocketModeClient with app B's `xapp` token → it receives 100% of app B's envelopes, proving app B had no other live connection despite the gateway claiming "connected (profile: b)".

## Root cause

`plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py`, `connect()`:

```python
raw_token = self.config.token              # bot token — profile-scoped ✓
app_token = os.getenv("SLACK_APP_TOKEN")   # app token — process env ✗
```

The bot token flows through per-profile platform config, but the app-level token is read straight from `os.environ`, which in a multiplexed gateway holds the **default** profile's `.env` values. So every secondary profile's adapter authenticates its WebSocket against the default profile's app.

`gateway/run.py::_profile_runtime_scope` explicitly documents the invariant this breaks:

> installs the profile's `.env` secrets as the authoritative credential source, so `get_secret` reads this profile's keys **and never the process-global `os.environ` (which in a multiplexer may hold another profile's values)**

The Slack adapter's `connect()` runs inside that scope (`_start_one_profile_adapters`), but bypasses it via `os.getenv`.

## Why it's invisible

- `apps.connections.open` succeeds with any valid `xapp` token, so every profile logs "Socket Mode connected".
- `auth.test` uses the (correctly scoped) bot token, so the logged identity per profile looks right.
- Slack delivers each envelope to one connection of the app it belongs to; apps with zero connections just drop events — no error surfaces on either side.
- The `_acquire_platform_lock("slack-app-token", …)` guard did not prevent five adapters connecting with the same app token in this setup.

## Suggested fix

Resolve the app token the same way as the bot token — through the profile-scoped secret path (e.g. `get_secret("SLACK_APP_TOKEN")` with `os.getenv` fallback for single-profile setups). A sweep of the adapter for other `os.getenv` reads of per-profile secrets (`SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS`, `SLACK_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, `SLACK_ALLOW_BOTS`, …) would catch the same class of leak where profiles legitimately differ.

## Related multiplex-isolation gaps (same class, can file separately if preferred)

1. **api_server enablement leaks + key presence implies enabled** (`gateway/config.py` ~1629): platform enablement reads `env_var_enabled("API_SERVER_ENABLED")` from process env and treats a present `API_SERVER_KEY` as "enabled", so secondary profiles inherit the default's api_server and crash the multiplexer with `MultiplexConfigError` unless all `API_SERVER_*` vars are stripped from every `.env` (workaround: move api_server to `platforms.api_server.extra` in config.yaml).
2. **`telegram_dm_topic_mode` / `telegram_dm_topic_bindings` have no profile dimension** (`hermes_state.py`): keyed by `(chat_id, user_id)` only, in the shared `state.db`. Under multiplex, all bots share the user's DM `chat_id`, so enabling `/topic` on one profile makes every other profile reply into a thread that only exists in the first profile's DM → `Message thread not found`, replies silently lost; binding rows also get overwritten across profiles.

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Description

In v0.18.0, the `_auto_sso_response()` function in `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py` auto-redirects unauthenticated dashboard visitors from `/` to `/auth/login?provider=basic` when BasicAuth is the only registered session provider. But `BasicAuthProvider.start_login()` raises `NotImplementedError` because it is password-only (the login page POSTs to `/auth/password-login`, not OAuth `start_login`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy Hermes v0.18.0 with password-only auth (no OAuth)
2. Set `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` and `_PASSWORD` env vars
3. Visit the dashboard URL in a browser with no existing session cookie
4. Result: 302 redirect to `/auth/login?provider=basic&next=%2F` → **500 Internal Server Error**

## Error

```
NotImplementedError: BasicAuthProvider is password-only; there is no OAuth redirect
flow. The login page POSTs to /auth/password-login instead.
```

## Workaround

Reverse proxy redirect rule: `GET /auth/login` → 302 → `/login`

## Expected Fix

Either:
- `_auto_sso_response()` should skip providers where `supports_password=True` and `start_login` is not supported
- OR `BasicAuthProvider.start_login()` should return a `LoginStart` that redirects to `/login` instead of raising

## Impact

Every password-only dashboard deployment is broken on unauthenticated first visit. Users cannot log in without a proxy workaround.

## Version

v0.18.0 (v2026.7.1)

items.title: v0.18.0: Discord silently broken after upgrade — plugin not auto-migrated, env not loaded, CMD mismatch
items.body:
## Description

In v0.18.0, the Discord platform was moved from a built-in gateway module to `plugins/platforms/discord/`. Existing v0.17.0 deployments lose Discord connectivity after upgrading with zero errors, warnings, or log messages.

## Root Causes

**A. Plugin not auto-enabled:** Discord moved to plugins. `plugins.enabled: []` in migrated config.yaml — must be `["discord"]`. Config migration does not add it.

**B. Env auto-loading changed:** `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` was previously auto-loaded from `~/.hermes/.env`, but in v0.18.0 this requires an explicit `env_file` directive in docker-compose or injection into the container environment.

**C. CMD mismatch:** If using `command: [dashboard, ...]` in docker-compose, the `_is_dashboard_container()` guard skips per-profile gateway reconciliation entirely, so the messaging gateway never starts. Must use `serve` or a non-dashboard CMD.

## Impact

Every Discord user upgrading from v0.17.0 loses bot connectivity with no visible errors. Discord shows "The application did not respond" as the only symptom.

## Expected

At minimum, the gateway should log a warning like "Discord platform enabled in config but DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN not found" or "Discord plugin not enabled." The config migration should auto-add `discord` to `plugins.enabled` when Discord was previously configured.

## Version

v0.18.0 (v2026.7.1)

items.title: computer-use should expose unverified CUA actions as a first-class status
items.body:
## Problem

`cua-driver` 0.7.0 exposes a richer action outcome than Hermes currently models. In addition to transport/tool failure (`isError`), action payloads can include:

```json
{
  "verified": false,
  "effect": "unverifiable",
  "path": "key_events"
}
```

That means the action was dispatched, but the driver could not confirm the target UI state changed. Hermes' `ActionResult` is currently binary (`ok: bool`), so the wrapper has to collapse this into either success or failure.

Bug fix #59730 makes the conservative choice for #59731: fail closed instead of reporting `verified:false` as confirmed success. That is safer, but it still loses useful semantics. A real macOS CUA smoke test showed why this matters: text landed in a disposable Tk text widget, but `cua-driver` still returned `verified:false` / `effect:"unverifiable"`. Hermes should be able to represent that as "dispatched but unverified," not just success vs failure.

Suggested labels: `type/feature`, `comp/tools`, `tool/mcp`, `P3`, `sweeper:blast-contained`

## Proposed Solution

Add a first-class action status/verification shape for `computer_use` action responses while preserving backward compatibility for existing callers that inspect `ok`.

A minimal model-facing shape could be:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "status": "unverified",
  "verified": false,
  "action": "type_text",
  "message": "Sent (unverified) 17 char(s) via CGEvent...",
  "meta": {
    "effect": "unverifiable",
    "path": "key_events"
  }
}
```

or, if maintainers prefer `ok` to mean "dispatched without transport error":

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "unverified",
  "verified": false,
  "action_dispatched": true,
  "action": "type_text",
  "meta": {"effect": "unverifiable", "path": "key_events"}
}
```

The important part is that `status: "unverified"` and `verified: false` are surfaced consistently and are not buried only in backend-specific `meta`.

## Alternatives

- Keep #59730's conservative binary behavior only: `verified:false` becomes `ok:false` and metadata explains why. This is safe, but treats "dispatched but unverified" like a hard failure.
- Keep current `ok:true` for `isError:false` and only surface metadata. This preserves driver dispatch semantics, but is misleading to the model/user because unverified actions look successful unless downstream code knows to inspect `meta.verified`.
- Add a broader tri-state result type to all `ActionResult` users, not only CUA. This is cleaner long term but has a wider blast radius.

## Evidence

- `trycua/cua` issue #2022 has been re-scoped after 0.7.0: CUA now returns `verified:false` / `effect:"unverifiable"` for pixel click uncertainty instead of a bare success message.
- `trycua/cua` issue #2058 similarly notes 0.7.0 surfaces `type_text` uncertainty as `verified:false` / `effect:"unverifiable"`.
- Hermes bug #59731 and draft PR #59730 document the current binary collapse and conservative fail-closed fix.
- A real CUA smoke test on macOS with a disposable Tk text window observed the typed text land while CUA still returned `verified:false`. This is exactly the semantic difference Hermes should preserve.

Debug report: not applicable; this is a design enhancement informed by isolated synthetic repro and disposable local GUI smoke tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `computer_use` action responses expose a first-class status for unverified actions, e.g. `status: "unverified"` plus `verified: false`.
- Existing binary `ok` behavior is documented and chosen deliberately.
- Regression tests cover at least one CUA action where `structuredContent.verified is False`.
- The result shape remains backward compatible enough that existing failure handling, especially `capture_after` skipping on non-confirmed actions, is not silently weakened.
- The implementation references #59731/#59730 and does not duplicate the bug-level fail-closed fix.

items.title: [Bug] Settings → Providers "remove key" doesn't fully remove provider — credential_pool persists across restart

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Environment
- OS: Windows 10
- App: Hermes Desktop (Hermes Agent)
- Observed: 2026-07-07

## Steps to reproduce
1. Add a provider via **Settings → Providers** (e.g. Xiaomi MiMo). This writes `XIAOMI_API_KEY` / `XIAOMI_BASE_URL` to `.env` and creates a `credential_pool` entry in `auth.json`.
2. Open **Settings → Providers**, locate the provider card, click the trash button on the key field.
3. Restart Hermes completely.
4. Open the model picker / Settings → Providers again.

## Expected behavior
The provider is fully removed: no entry in `auth.json` `credential_pool`, and no models in the picker.

## Actual behavior
The provider **reappears** in the model picker after restart. Investigation:
- `.env` key is correctly commented out by the GUI (✓).
- BUT `auth.json` → `credential_pool["xiaomi"]` is **NOT removed**.
- `provider_models_cache.json` still caches the provider's models.

## Root cause
The GUI "remove key" handler only mutates `.env` (comments out the key). It does **not** prune the corresponding `credential_pool` entry in `auth.json`. On startup the `credential_pool` loader is **additive-only** — it adds providers discovered from `.env` but never prunes entries whose env key is gone. So the stale `credential_pool` entry survives the restart and re-populates the provider/model list.

## Workaround (verified)
Manually delete the provider key from `auth.json` `credential_pool` and remove it from `provider_models_cache.json`, then restart. Deleting the `.env` key alone (via GUI or by hand) is **not sufficient**.

## Suggested fix
When the Settings → Providers trash button removes a key, it should also remove the matching `credential_pool` entry (and refresh model caches) so "delete provider" completes in one action.

*(Reported by a Chinese user; root cause confirmed by inspecting `auth.json` + cache files after a clean GUI delete + restart.)*

items.title: kanban_complete` goal-mode judge gate never rejects: 3-target unpack of 4-tuple `judge_goal()` raises `ValueError`, caught by the fail-open handler

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
## Title

`kanban_complete` goal-mode judge gate never rejects: 3-target unpack of 4-tuple `judge_goal()` raises `ValueError`, caught by the fail-open handler

## Affected version

- hermes-agent **0.18.0** (`pyproject.toml`, `[project] version = "0.18.0"`)
- Install: git checkout of `main` @ `3ba5ba89c2479b04466a3cb2f6b14b1f6e8f164c` (2026-07-06)
- Platform: macOS (darwin), Python 3.11–3.13 per `requires-python`

## Summary

The pre-completion judge gate added for goal-mode tasks (code comment cites Issue #38367, `tools/kanban_tools.py:595`) is dead code in practice. It unpacks `judge_goal()` into **three** targets, but `judge_goal()` returns a **four**-element tuple. The resulting `ValueError` is swallowed by the gate's own defensive `except Exception`, which was written for a different failure mode, and completion is allowed unconditionally.

## The logic, reproduced from the install

`tools/kanban_tools.py:600-624` (inside `_handle_complete`):

```python
task = kb.get_task(conn, tid)
if task and task.goal_mode and _goal_judge_available():
    verdict = "done"
    reason = ""
    try:
        verdict, reason, _ = judge_goal(                     # <-- line 605: 3 targets
            goal=f"{task.title}\n\n{task.body or ''}".strip(),
            last_response=(summary or result or "").strip(),
        )
    except Exception as judge_exc:
        # Defensive: judge_goal swallows its own errors, but if
        # it ever raises, fail open rather than wedge the worker.
        logger.warning(
            "goal judge check failed, allowing completion: %s",
            judge_exc,
            exc_info=True,
        )
    if verdict != "done":
        return tool_error(
            f"Goal completion rejected by judge: {reason}. ..."
        )
```

`hermes_cli/goals.py:836-844` — the callee's signature:

```python
def judge_goal(
    goal: str,
    last_response: str,
    *,
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_JUDGE_TIMEOUT,
    subgoals: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    background_processes: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
    contract: Optional[GoalContract] = None,
) -> Tuple[str, str, bool, Optional[Dict[str, Any]]]:
```

Every return path in `judge_goal` is a 4-tuple `(verdict, reason, parse_failed, wait_directive)` — early exits at `goals.py:875, 878, 884, 890, 893, 951` and the main return at `goals.py:964`. There is no 3-tuple path.

So at `kanban_tools.py:605`:

1. `judge_goal(...)` returns e.g. `("continue", "no test evidence", False, None)`.
2. `verdict, reason, _ = <4-tuple>` raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`.
3. The `except Exception as judge_exc` at line 609 catches it and logs
   `goal judge check failed, allowing completion: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`.
4. `verdict` still holds its line-602 initializer `"done"`, so the line-617 rejection branch never fires.
5. `kb.complete_task(...)` runs — the card completes no matter what the judge said.

Note this is the *opposite* of the intended fail-open design: `_goal_judge_available()` (`kanban_tools.py:185-203`) exists precisely so the gate only enforces **when a judge is reachable**. With this bug, the gate is bypassed exactly in the case it was supposed to enforce. It also silently undermines the sibling `kanban_block` gate (code comment at `kanban_tools.py:691-700`, Issue #38696), whose rationale is that disallowed block kinds "route back through kanban_complete, which the judge now gates" — it does not.

## Minimal repro

1. Configure any auxiliary model for the `goal_judge` slot (so `_goal_judge_available()` is True).
2. Create a goal-mode card with a concrete acceptance criterion:
   ```bash
   hermes kanban create --title "Judge gate probe" \
     --body "Acceptance: paste the passing output of 'pytest tests/x'." \
     --goal-mode
   ```
3. As the worker for that task (`HERMES_KANBAN_TASK=<id>`), call the tool with a summary that plainly fails the criterion:
   ```
   kanban_complete(summary="did nothing, no tests were run")
   ```

Or, without a board at all, demonstrate the crash directly:

```python
from hermes_cli.goals import judge_goal
verdict, reason, _ = judge_goal(goal="x", last_response="y")   # same unpack as kanban_tools.py:605
# ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)
```

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** `tool_error("Goal completion rejected by judge: ...")` — the worker is told to provide acceptance evidence or create continuation tasks.
- **Actual:** the task completes. The only trace is a `logger.warning("goal judge check failed, allowing completion: too many values to unpack (expected 3)")` in the worker log. On the board the completion looks judge-approved.

## Suggested fix

Unpack all four elements at `tools/kanban_tools.py:605`:

```python
verdict, reason, _parse_failed, _wait = judge_goal(
    goal=f"{task.title}\n\n{task.body or ''}".strip(),
    last_response=(summary or result or "").strip(),
)
```

Plus, to keep this from regressing:

- Add a unit test that stubs `judge_goal` to return `("continue", "why", False, None)` and asserts `kanban_complete` returns the rejection `tool_error` (the current defensive `except` made the breakage invisible to the existing suite).
- Consider logging at `error` (not `warning`) when the gate's own code raises, and/or narrowing the defensive `except` — it was meant for judge transport failures, and `judge_goal` already fail-opens those internally (returns `"continue"` instead of raising, `goals.py:870-872, 949-951`).
- Decide explicitly how the gate treats a `"wait"` verdict (currently any non-`"done"` verdict rejects; that is probably fine but worth stating).

## Workaround we deployed

We treat the completion gate as nonexistent and enforce completion outside it, in layers:

1. **Deterministic verification in the lane wrappers** — each dispatched card can carry a `verify:` shell command; the worker wrapper re-runs it after the run and marks the result failed on nonzero exit (rules-based gate, no LLM).
2. **In-run Stop-hook judge** on our Claude Code lane — a Stop hook re-runs the verify command and blocks the model from stopping (with the failure output as the next instruction) until it passes or a self-cap is hit.
3. The **per-turn goal-loop judge** (`run_kanban_goal_loop` path, which calls `judge_goal` with correct arity) still functions and remains the fuzzy end-state check; card bodies carry judge-checkable acceptance criteria with an explicit evidence section.

i.e. we rely on nothing from the `kanban_complete` gate until this is fixed upstream.
