items.title: [Bug]: _summarize_api_error crashes with httpx.ResponseNotRead on Gemini streaming errors, hiding the real message (e.g. free-tier quota 429s)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

`_summarize_api_error()` in `run_agent.py` crashes with `httpx.ResponseNotRead` while trying to build a human-readable summary of a `GeminiAPIError` raised from a streaming call. This happens on *every* conversation turn when the underlying Gemini call fails (in my case: a 429 free-tier quota exhaustion), so the real, already-computed, actionable error message is thrown away and replaced with:

```
Attempted to access streaming response content, without having called `read()`.
```

This makes a simple "your API key has no quota" problem look like the whole agent is broken, since the message repeats identically on every single turn with no indication of the real cause.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Google AI Studio key that has no quota for the model in use (e.g. a free-tier key returns `generate_content_free_tier_requests, limit: 0` for `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`).
2. Send any message in a chat session (CLI or Desktop).
3. The native Gemini streaming call gets a `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` from Google.
4. `_stream_completion()` in `agent/gemini_native_adapter.py` correctly reads the error body via the bounded reader (`read_streaming_error_body`) and raises `GeminiAPIError` with a fully-formed message (including the free-tier billing guidance) — but does not set a `.body` attribute on the exception.
5. `_summarize_api_error()` in `run_agent.py` checks `getattr(error, "body", None)` first (not set here), falls through, then does `getattr(error.response, "text", None)` on the *same* streaming `httpx.Response` — which raises `httpx.ResponseNotRead` because the body was consumed via `iter_bytes()` (not `.read()`) and the response was already closed.
6. That secondary exception propagates up through `agent/conversation_loop.py::run_conversation` (~line 2949) and replaces the original, useful error.

### Expected Behavior

The turn should surface the real Gemini error message that `GeminiAPIError` already computed (e.g. the 429 + free-tier billing guidance), not crash while trying to summarize it.

### Actual Behavior

Every turn fails with the generic streaming-read error instead of the real message that was already built and discarded:

```
Gemini HTTP 429 (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED): You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. For more information on this error, head to: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits. To monitor your current usage, head to: https://ai.dev/rate-limit.
* Quota exceeded for metric: generativelanguage.googleapis.com/generate_content_free_tier_input_token_count, limit: 0, model: gemini-3.1-pro
* Quota exceeded for metric: generativelanguage.googleapis.com/generate_content_free_tier_requests, limit: 0, model: gemini-3.1-pro
Please retry in 25.239541983s.

Your Google API key is on the free tier (<= 250 requests/day for gemini-2.5-flash). Hermes typically makes 3-10 API calls per user turn, so the free tier is exhausted in a handful of messages and cannot sustain an agent session. Enable billing on your Google Cloud project and regenerate the key in a billing-enabled project: https://aistudio.google.com/apikey
```

Occurred identically on both `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` and `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` (both `provider=gemini`, `platform=tui`), and separately inside `agent/background_review.py`'s background memory/skill review job — same exception, caught there and only logged (so it doesn't crash the review), but it still discards the real cause via the same `_summarize_api_error` path.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Debug Report

Didn't run `hermes debug share` for this report (would upload local config to a third-party paste service). Full local traceback from `~/.hermes/logs/tui_gateway_crash.log` below, with the local home directory path redacted to `~`.

### Operating System

macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)

### Additional Logs / Traceback

```
agent.gemini_native_adapter.GeminiAPIError: Gemini HTTP 429 (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED): You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. For more information on this error, head to: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits. To monitor your current usage, head to: https://ai.dev/rate-limit.
* Quota exceeded for metric: generativelanguage.googleapis.com/generate_content_free_tier_input_token_count, limit: 0, model: gemini-3.1-pro
* Quota exceeded for metric: generativelanguage.googleapis.com/generate_content_free_tier_requests, limit: 0, model: gemini-3.1-pro
Please retry in 25.239541983s.

Your Google API key is on the free tier (<= 250 requests/day for gemini-2.5-flash). Hermes typically makes 3-10 API calls per user turn, so the free tier is exhausted in a handful of messages and cannot sustain an agent session. Enable billing on your Google Cloud project and regenerate the key in a billing-enabled project: https://aistudio.google.com/apikey

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "~/.hermes/hermes-agent/tui_gateway/server.py", line 8674, in run
    result = agent.run_conversation(run_message, **run_kwargs)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "~/.hermes/hermes-agent/run_agent.py", line 5758, in run_conversation
    return run_conversation(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "~/.hermes/hermes-agent/agent/conversation_loop.py", line 2949, in run_conversation
    _error_summary = agent._summarize_api_error(api_error)
                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "~/.hermes/hermes-agent/run_agent.py", line 2146, in _summarize_api_error
    snippet = (getattr(response, "text", None) or "").strip()
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_models.py", line 644, in text
    content = self.content
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_models.py", line 638, in content
    raise ResponseNotRead()
httpx.ResponseNotRead: Attempted to access streaming response content, without having called `read()`.
```

### Root Cause Analysis

- `agent/gemini_native_adapter.py::_stream_completion` (~line 973) already reads the error body safely via the bounded reader before raising:
  ```python
  if response.status_code != 200:
      body_text = read_streaming_error_body(response)
      raise gemini_http_error(response, body_text=body_text)
  ```
- `gemini_http_error()` (~line 745) builds a complete, human-readable `message` from that `body_text` (including the free-tier guidance) and passes it to `GeminiAPIError.__init__`, but only stores `response=response` on the exception — it never sets a `.body` dict, unlike other error paths in the codebase (e.g. `_StreamErrorEvent` in `run_agent.py` ~line 353, which explicitly sets `.body` so that "`_summarize_api_error` / `_extract_api_error_context` / `classify_api_error` all pick it up").
- `run_agent.py::_summarize_api_error` (~line 2098) checks `getattr(error, "body", None)` first — not present on `GeminiAPIError` — then falls through to the branch at ~line 2144 which does `getattr(response, "text", None)` directly on `error.response`. Since that response body was consumed via `iter_bytes()` (not `.read()`) inside `read_streaming_error_body` and then closed, accessing `.text` raises `httpx.ResponseNotRead` instead of returning the text that was already known.
- `agent/error_classifier.py::_extract_error_body` has the same shape of raw `response.json()` call on `error.response`, but wraps it in `try/except Exception: pass`, so it degrades gracefully instead of crashing. `_summarize_api_error`'s equivalent branch has no such guard.

### Proposed Fix

Either (or both):

1. Have `gemini_http_error()` set the already-computed `body_text` as `details["body_text"]` (or a proper `body=` dict, matching `_StreamErrorEvent`'s shape) on `GeminiAPIError`, so `_summarize_api_error`'s existing, working `body` branch handles it and never touches `.response.text`.
2. Wrap the `response.text` access in `run_agent.py::_summarize_api_error` (~line 2144) in `try/except Exception`, matching the defensive pattern already used in `agent/error_classifier.py::_extract_error_body`.

(2) is the smaller, more general fix — it protects every current and future caller of `_summarize_api_error` against any provider that raises an error carrying an unread streaming `httpx.Response`, not just Gemini.

items.title: 关于Hermes快捷方式或者任务栏图标有时候图标会变为Electron的问题

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## 问题描述

Windows 桌面版 Hermes：任务栏图标显示 Electron 默认图标（深色圆底 + 白色节点网络），而非 Hermes logo。右键任务栏弹出菜单也显示 "Electron"。

安装后首次启动图标正常，之后变为 Electron 默认图标。

## 原因分析

Windows `.lnk` 快捷方式的图标与 `.exe` 内嵌资源图标是独立的。Hermes 打包时将正确图标置于 `resources/icon.ico`，但任务栏快捷方式偶尔会回退到 Electron 框架的默认图标。

## 复现步骤

1. 安装 Hermes 桌面版
2. 固定到任务栏
3. 重启几次后任务栏图标变为 Electron 默认图标

## 临时修复方法

1. 右键**图标正确**的快捷方式 → 属性 → 更改图标 → 复制"查找此文件中的图标"路径
2. 右键**图标错误**的任务栏快捷方式 → 属性 → 更改图标 → 粘贴路径 → 选择 Hermes 图标
3. 确定 → 重启 Hermes
4. 补充：就算把桌面原生生成的快捷方式直接拖到任务栏也无法解决

正确图标路径参考：
```
%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\apps\desktop\release\win-unpacked\resources\icon.ico
```

## 建议修复方向

构建脚本中确保 Windows 快捷方式 (.lnk) 的 `IconLocation` 显式指向 `resources/icon.ico`，而非依赖 exe 内嵌资源。或者设置 `app.setAppUserModelId('com.nousresearch.hermes')` 确保任务栏识别正确的应用身份。

## 环境

- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Hermes 版本: 当前 main 分支

items.title: [Bug]: honcho_conclude delete_id is unreachable — no tool exposes a real conclusion id

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
## What

`honcho_conclude`'s delete action (`delete_id`) is unusable in practice: the model has no way to
ever obtain a real conclusion `id` before calling it, because no tool in the Honcho plugin exposes
Honcho's conclusion-search/list endpoints.

### Root cause

Honcho's Python SDK already implements everything needed — `ConclusionScope.list()` and
`ConclusionScope.query()` in `honcho/conclusions.py` (hitting the server's
`POST /v3/workspaces/{ws}/conclusions/list` and `POST /v3/workspaces/{ws}/conclusions/query`
routes), both of which return real `Conclusion` objects with a populated string `id` field.

But none of the 5 tool schemas/handlers in `plugins/memory/honcho/__init__.py` ever call either
method:

- `honcho_search` → `session.py` `search_context()` → SDK's `peer.context(search_query=...)`.
  This hits Honcho's peer-context/representation endpoint and returns synthesized representation
  text + peer-card fact strings — never `Conclusion` objects, so no `.id` ever flows through this
  path. It searches the **Message** resource space, not Conclusions — a completely separate ID
  space.
- `honcho_conclude` (delete) reads `delete_id` from the model's tool call and forwards it verbatim
  to the SDK's `ConclusionScope.delete()`, which just does a bare
  `DELETE /v3/workspaces/{ws}/conclusions/{conclusion_id}`. No numeric-ID requirement anywhere —
  it's a plain string passthrough that works fine *if* given a real id.
- `honcho_profile`, `honcho_context`, `honcho_reasoning` — checked, none of these touch conclusions
  either.

So the model is asked to supply `delete_id` but is never given any tool that could produce one.
`Conclusion.id` is a nanoid string (server-generated, `generate_nanoid` default in the Honcho
server's model), not a numeric ID — the ID format itself was never the problem.

### Fix (PR attached)

Add a `list` mode to the existing `honcho_conclude` tool, backed by a new
`HonchoSessionManager.list_conclusions()` that wraps the SDK's `ConclusionScope.query()` (when a
search query is given) or `.list()` (to browse recent conclusions), mapping results to
`{"id": ..., "content": ...}`. This unblocks the intended flow: list/search → read a real id →
delete. No new tool is added, and no existing method signature changes.

## How to Test

1. Call `honcho_conclude(conclusion="some fact")` to create a conclusion.
2. Call `honcho_conclude(list=true)` (optionally with a `query`) — confirm the response includes
   the conclusion's real `id`.
3. Call `honcho_conclude(delete_id=<that id>)` — confirm it succeeds.
4. Call `honcho_conclude(list=true)` again — confirm the deleted conclusion no longer appears.

## Type
Bug

## Related
- Distinct from #59469 / #59470 (dialectic char-cap clipping and `reasoning_level` schema
  guidance, both fixed in #59471 / #59472) — this is a separate root cause (missing tool/tool-path)
  rather than a data-handling issue in an existing path.
- #52395 (draft, "General improvements and Fixes to Honcho memory integration") touches
  `search_context()` and tool descriptions in the same two files, but different regions —
  verified no overlap with this fix.
- #37759 and #42815 are separate `honcho_conclude` bugs (create-path peer routing, and
  `peer_id`/`observer_id`+`observed_id` payload mismatch respectively) — unrelated to this
  lookup gap, noted here only to avoid confusion with "honcho_conclude is broken" search hits.

items.title: [Feature]:  Float16 semantic memory provider with automatic turn capture

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case


Hermes builtin memory uses FTS5 keyword search. `What database do we use?`
cannot find `we migrated to Postgres` because the word `database` isn't in the
stored text. The semantic gap — different words, same meaning — is 0% recall.

Every existing memory provider (Honcho, Mem0, Holographic, etc.) stores raw
text or uncompressed float32 embeddings. None compress storage. None do
semantic retrieval by default. None auto-capture conversations without the
agent explicitly calling `memory add`.

Users with long-running sessions or multiple projects cannot reliably find past
conversations unless they remember the exact keywords used.

### Proposed Solution

New memory provider under `plugins/memory/kv_memory/`:

- Encodes every turn into a 384-dim embedding via sentence-transformers
  (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 80MB, CPU-only, ~5ms per turn)
- Stores as float16 (2 bytes/element) in SQLite with WAL mode — 2x compression
  vs FP32 with zero retrieval quality loss (Kendall tau 0.99)
- Retrieves by cosine similarity — "database" finds "Postgres" even when the
  word "database" was never used
- Captures every turn automatically via `post_llm_call` hook — no `memory add`
  or `--yolo` required
- Exposes two tools: `kv_memory_search(query, limit)` and `kv_memory_status()`

**config.yaml**
memory:
  provider: kv_memory
plugins:
  kv_memory:
    embedding_backend: auto    # auto | sentence-transformers | api
    top_k: 5
    storage_mode: fp16         # fp16 (safe, 2x) or q4 (aggressive, 4-7x)

Pure plugin. Zero core Hermes changes. Single pip dependency.



### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Feature Type

Performance / reliability

### Scope

None

### Contribution

- [x] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

```shell

```

items.title: Feature: native Slack cron delivery mode for headline top-level post + threaded body
items.body:
## Feature Description

Add first-class Slack cron delivery support for **headline-only top-level post + detailed threaded follow-up**.

Today, long weekly reports are too noisy as top-level Slack posts, but Hermes cron currently has no reliable native way to:
1. post a one-line top-level message,
2. capture the returned Slack `ts`, and
3. post the full body into that newly created thread.

This should be a Hermes feature rather than a per-job prompt hack or timing workaround.

## Motivation

A common reporting pattern is:
- **top-level channel post:** one-line headline only
- **thread reply:** full report/details

Without this, users must choose between two bad options:
- giant wall-of-text top-level posts, or
- brittle thread targeting that depends on stale thread IDs / ad hoc sender behavior.

In our weekly Android report flow, the top-level post needs to stay very short, and the full weekly report belongs in-thread.

## Current Behavior / Gaps

Current Hermes behavior exposes several gaps:
- `cronjob(deliver=slack:<channel>)` can create a fresh top-level Slack post from the final response.
- But Hermes does **not** provide a reliable native way to send a second auto-threaded follow-up tied to that newly created post.
- Existing Slack targeting/thread behavior is already shaky enough that users should not have to hack around it in prompts.

Related issues:
- #59097 — stale thread context can hijack async/cron Slack delivery
- #9394 — standalone Slack sends ignore or mishandle thread context

## Proposed Solution

Add a native Slack delivery mode for cron (and possibly general message delivery) that explicitly supports a **two-step threaded report**.

### Option A: explicit structured fields

Example shape:

```json
{
  "deliver": "slack:C0BDB6GP56F",
  "delivery_mode": "headline_then_thread",
  "headline": "Android weekly update — week ending 2026-07-03",
  "body": "<full weekly report>"
}
```

Runtime behavior:
1. `chat.postMessage(channel=..., text=headline)`
2. capture returned `ts`
3. `chat.postMessage(channel=..., thread_ts=<ts>, text=body)`

### Option B: final response contract

Hermes cron could interpret the final response as:
- **first line** → top-level Slack post
- **remaining lines** → threaded reply

This is less explicit than Option A, but still far better than today if implemented natively.

## Reliability Requirements

This should be implemented as a runtime feature, not a prompt workaround.

Requirements:
- no dependence on stale stored thread IDs
- no blind `sleep`/wait as the primary mechanism
- thread reply must use the **actual `ts` returned by the top-level post**
- if the threaded follow-up fails, surface that clearly in cron job status / delivery errors
- ideally keep the top-level headline posted even if the thread body fails

## Nice-to-have Behavior

- return/store both the top-level `ts` and the thread follow-up result in cron delivery metadata
- optionally support the same behavior from `send_message` or other async delivery paths
- allow future platform-specific variants (e.g. Discord forum/thread follow-up patterns)

## Alternatives Considered

### 1. Put the full report in the top-level post
Rejected — too noisy for channel UX.

### 2. Precompute or persist a thread ID
Rejected — does not satisfy the “new thread each run” requirement.

### 3. Add waits / retries only
Rejected as the main solution — timing is not the real product abstraction. The needed primitive is: **post, capture ts, reply in thread**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A cron job can reliably create a **new top-level Slack post** each run.
- The same cron run can reliably post the **full body as a reply in that new thread**.
- The feature does not require users to hand-roll Slack-specific prompt hacks.
- Delivery metadata and errors make it obvious whether the headline post succeeded, whether the threaded body succeeded, and what `ts/thread_ts` were used.

items.title: [Bug] Cron scheduler silently fails (no Discord delivery) — absolute skill paths rejected by skill_view path-security check

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Symptom

When cron jobs are scheduled (via the bundle operator workflow that creates them with `setup-cron-jobs.sh` or equivalent), the scheduler runs them on schedule but every tick logs:

```
WARNING cron.scheduler: Cron job '<name>': skill not found, skipping — Skill '<absolute-path>' not found.
```

The cron continues, calls the LLM with no skill context, and delivers a degraded/empty response to Discord — or nothing at all. **The user-visible symptom**: "the audit channel went silent after <time>".

This was hit on a Contabo production VPS (2026-07-06): a cron-driven scalp scanner (M3 + M11) sits silent in the audit channel because every cron tick''s skill loads fail.

## Root cause

`cron/jobs.json` stores skills as **absolute paths**, e.g.:

```json
{
  "skills": [
    "/home/hermes/agent-trading-skills/SKILLS/market-context/market-regime-detection/",
    "/home/hermes/agent-trading-skills/SKILLS/market-context/pre-market-scanning/",
    ...
  ]
}
```

But `tools/skills_tool.py::_skill_lookup_path_error()` rejects any absolute path:

```python
def _skill_lookup_path_error(name: str) -> Optional[str]:
    ...
    if (
        PurePosixPath(candidate).is_absolute()
        or PureWindowsPath(candidate).is_absolute()
        or PureWindowsPath(candidate).drive
    ):
        return "Skill name must be a relative path within the skills directory."
```

So `skill_view("/home/hermes/agent-trading-skills/SKILLS/market-context/market-regime-detection/")` always returns `{"success": false, "error": "Skill name must be a relative path within the skills directory."}`. The scheduler then logs `Skill not found, skipping`, all N skills in the cron job fail to load, and the LLM gets called with no skill context.

## How to reproduce (on the operator side)

```bash
# On the VPS:
cat /home/hermes/.hermes/profiles/quant-sigma/cron/jobs.json
# observe: `"skills"` entries are absolute paths starting with /home/hermes/.../SKILLS/

journalctl --user -u hermes-gateway-quant-sigma --since "today" | grep "skill not found"
# observe: N skills × M cron ticks = dozens of "skill not found, skipping" warnings
```

## Suggested fix (happy to iterate)

Relax `_skill_lookup_path_error` to allow absolute paths that resolve to the trusted skills directory. The path-security check should:

1. Allow absolute paths that start with any of `$HERMES_HOME/skills/`, `~/.hermes/skills/`, `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/skills/` (the latter via the SKILLS symlink farm)
2. STILL reject paths that escape the skills directory (preserve the traversal-component check)
3. Still reject Windows-style drive paths
4. Strip the prefix and resolve as a relative path downstream

Alternatively, fix the operator-side setup (`scripts/setup-cron-jobs.sh` in whatever bundle generates the cron job config) to use **bare skill names** (`market-context/market-regime-detection`) instead of absolute paths.

## Diagnostic data (from the operator''s VPS, 2026-07-06)

```bash
$ cat ~/.hermes/profiles/quant-sigma/cron/jobs.json | head -25
{
    "jobs": [{
        "id": "8aebc0f21dc2",
        "name": "opportunity-scanner",
        "skills": [
            "/home/hermes/agent-trading-skills/SKILLS/market-context/market-regime-detection/",
            "/home/hermes/agent-trading-skills/SKILLS/market-context/pre-market-scanning/",
            ...
        ],
        "skill": "/home/hermes/agent-trading-skills/SKILLS/market-context/market-regime-detection/",
        ...
        "schedule": {"kind": "cron", "expr": "30 8 * * 1-5", "display": "30 8 * * 1-5"},
        "next_run_at": "2026-07-07T08:30:00-04:00",
    },
    ...
}

$ journalctl --user -u hermes-gateway-quant-sigma --since "today" | grep "skill not found" | wc -l
142

$ journalctl --user -u hermes-gateway-quant-sigma --since "today" | grep "skill not found" | head -3
Jul 06 14:30:33 ... WARNING cron.scheduler: Cron job ''opportunity-scanner'': skill not found, skipping — Skill ''SKILLS/market-context/market-regime-detection/'' not found.
Jul 06 14:30:33 ... WARNING cron.scheduler: Cron job ''opportunity-scanner'': skill not found, skipping — Skill ''SKILLS/market-context/pre-market-scanning/'' not found.
Jul 06 14:30:33 ... WARNING cron.scheduler: Cron job ''opportunity-scanner'': skill not found, skipping — Skill ''SKILLS/market-context/multi-timeframe-analysis/'' not found.
```

## Two lower-priority cosmetic issues found during the same investigation

1. `hermes cron list` displays `next_run_at` + `last_run_at` with the system-local TZ label (e.g. `+02:00 CEST`) instead of the schedule''s intended TZ (e.g. `-04:00 EDT` for a 9-15 ET schedule). The absolute time is correct, just the label is wrong. Cosmetically confusing.

2. The scheduler computes the next run via `croniter(expr, base_time)` where `base_time` is `_hermes_now()`. If the system clock is not aligned with the cron schedule''s intended TZ, the cron schedule would silently shift (currently CEST offset = 6h from EDT, which happens to align the cron schedule correctly to "9-15 ET" for this specific deployment — but it would break when DST changes or if the VPS TZ changes).

Both are tractable: use `_resolve_timezone_name()` + `ZoneInfo` when constructing the croniter base_time, display the same TZ in `hermes cron list`.

## Why the existing symlink work didn''t catch this

A previous fix (commit `e2d7e58` + followups) did create a skills symlink:
- `~/.hermes/profiles/quant-sigma/skills/SKILLS → /home/hermes/agent-trading-skills/SKILLS`

But the cron job config still stores absolute paths as the skill identifier. The symlink lets `skill_view(SKILLS/...)` work IF called with the relative path, but the scheduler calls with the absolute path (per the job config), which the path-security check rejects.

Severity: **silent failure in production** — the user-visible "audit channel goes silent" symptom is hard to debug from logs alone because the cron appears healthy (`Last run: ok`).

items.title: Hermes Mnemosyne plugin sets auto_sleep default to false, breaking cross-session memory consolidation

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

The Hermes integration plugin for Mnemosyne (`integrations/hermes/src/mnemosyne_hermes/__init__.py`) sets `auto_sleep` to `false` by default (line 662), overriding the Mnemosyne core default of `true`. This means Mnemosyne never automatically consolidates working memory into episodic memory, effectively breaking cross-session memory retrieval for fresh Hermes+Mnemosyne installations.

A user can write memories, but recall across sessions never returns meaningful results because the episodic vector index stays empty.

## Root Cause

In `__init__.py`, the `get_config_schema()` method defines:
```python
{"key": "auto_sleep", "description": "...", "default": False},
```

Mnemosyne core documentation states the default should be `true` — consolidation runs on session start and end. But the Hermes plugin imposes `false` with no notice, no setup wizard prompt, and no mention in the installation docs.

## Impact

- Fresh install: memory appears to work but never consolidates
- Users discover it only when they notice the agent keeps forgetting cross-session context
- Workaround: manually set `memory.mnemosyne.auto_sleep: true` in config.yaml (and optionally `sleep_threshold: 20`)
- A cron job may still be needed for `mnemosyne sleep --all-sessions` to clean up historical unconsolidated data

## Expected

The Hermes plugin should either:
1. Default `auto_sleep` to `true` to match Mnemosyne core defaults, OR
2. Prompt during `hermes setup` or first-run to let the user opt in

## Environment

- Hermes version: current main branch (git-based install)
- Mnemosyne version: 3.10.0
- Platform: macOS
- Config: `memory.provider: mnemosyne`, no `auto_sleep` in default config

## Relevant Code

`integrations/hermes/src/mnemosyne_hermes/__init__.py:662`:
```python
{"key": "auto_sleep", "description": "Auto-run sleep() when working memory exceeds threshold. Set true to enable. Backward-compatible with MNEMOSYNE_AUTO_SLEEP_ENABLED env var.", "default": False},
```

`integrations/hermes/src/mnemosyne_hermes/__init__.py:352-353`:
```python
self._auto_sleep_threshold = 50
self._auto_sleep_enabled = os.environ.get("MNEMOSYNE_AUTO_SLEEP_ENABLED", "").strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")
```

items.title: [Bug] Kanban task event notifications never delivered — all 18 subscriptions have last_event_id=0

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

`kanban_notify_subs` subscriptions are created correctly when a task is dispatched, but the Gateway never delivers any task event notifications to the originating conversation. **18 subscriptions, 29 terminal events, 0 deliveries.**

## Environment

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **Version** | v0.18.0 (2026.7.1), upstream `83016547` |
| **OS** | Windows 10 (native, not Docker/WSL) |
| **Interface** | Desktop GUI (WebUI) + TUI (both affected) |
| **Gateway** | Running, PID 22344 |
| **Config** | `kanban.dispatch_in_gateway: true`, `dispatch_interval_seconds: 10` |
| **DB** | `kanban.db` (SQLite), table `kanban_notify_subs` |

## Expected Behavior

Per documentation: when `kanban_create` is called from a gateway conversation, the conversation is auto-subscribed. When the worker calls `kanban_block()` or `kanban_complete()`, the Gateway should poll `task_events`, match the subscription, and push a notification back to the originating conversation.

## Actual Behavior

**No notification is ever delivered.** The `kanban_notify_subs` table records subscriptions correctly, but `last_event_id` remains `0` for every single row.

## Evidence

### Database state

- Total subscriptions: **18**
- Subscriptions with `last_event_id > 0`: **0** (never delivered)
- Terminal events (blocked/completed): **29**
- Total events: **260**

### Platform breakdown

| Platform | Subscriptions | Delivered |
|----------|:---:|:---:|
| `api_server` (WebUI) | 2 | 0 |
| `tui` | 16 | 0 |

### Sample: terminal events with zero delivery

| Task | Event | last_event_id | Platform |
|------|-------|:---:|----------|
| `t_9146c964` | blocked | 0 | api_server |
| `t_dfb8cda8` | blocked | 0 | api_server |
| `t_312dc3ca` | blocked | 0 | tui |
| `t_84f17f38` | completed | 0 | tui |
| `t_6c786509` | completed | 0 | tui |

## Reproduction

1. Open a WebUI session
2. `kanban_create(title="test", assignee=<any>, body="kanban_block('test')")` → returns `subscribed: true` ✅
3. Wait for worker to execute → `task_events` records event ✅, subscription row exists ✅
4. **Notification never appears** 🔴 — `last_event_id` stays `0`
5. Wait > `gateway_notify_interval` (180s) — still nothing

## Impact

- Orchestrator agents cannot rely on event-driven notification
- Pipeline automation requires manual `kanban_show()` polling
- Users relying on documented auto-notify behavior are silently broken

## Possible Root Cause

The Gateway notification poller either:
1. Does not query the `kanban_notify_subs` table
2. Matches events but fails to deliver to `api_server`/`tui` platforms
3. Has a platform dispatch path that is unimplemented for non-messaging channels

items.title: [Feature] Hermes Studio: bring Kanban to primary navigation

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Problem

In Hermes Studio (WebUI), the Kanban board is buried under the Settings sidebar as a secondary page. To check task status, I have to:

1. Open Settings
2. Find Kanban in the settings sidebar
3. Click into it

This makes Kanban feel like a configuration tool rather than a first-class workflow feature. Given that Hermes promotes multi-agent collaboration via Kanban, it deserves primary visibility.

## Proposal

Move the Kanban entry from the Settings sidebar to the **primary navigation** — either as a top-level tab or pinned in the main sidebar alongside Sessions / Workflows / Settings.

## Why

- Kanban is a core collaboration feature, not a setting

items.title: Crash: "AttributeError: NoneType object has no attribute get" in /journey when skill frontmatter has metadata: null

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

`/journey` (Hermes Studio learning graph, `hermes journey` CLI) crashes with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` when any installed skill's `SKILL.md` frontmatter has `metadata` set to `null` or `metadata: {hermes: null}`.

## Error Traceback

```
File "agent/learning_graph.py", line 61, in _category
    cat = fm.get("category") or (fm.get("metadata", {}).get("hermes", {}) or {}).get("category")
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
```

## Root Cause

In `agent/learning_graph.py`, both `_category()` (line 61) and `_related()` (line 52) use:

```python
fm.get("metadata", {}).get("hermes", {})
```

Python's `dict.get(key, default)` only returns the default when the key is **absent**. If `metadata` key **exists** in the frontmatter but its value is `null`, `.get("metadata", {})` returns `None`, then `None.get("hermes", {})` raises `AttributeError`.

This can happen when:
- A skill's frontmatter has `metadata:` followed by nothing or `null` in YAML
- `metadata: {hermes: null}` (inner `.get("hermes", {})` also returns `None`)

## Fix Already on `main`

Commit `05cbddc` introduced the `_hermes_meta()` helper:

```python
def _hermes_meta(fm: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    meta = fm.get("metadata")
    hermes = meta.get("hermes") if isinstance(meta, dict) else None
    return hermes if isinstance(hermes, dict) else {}
```

This guards against `metadata=None`, `metadata=<string>`, and `metadata.hermes=None`. The fix will ship in the next release.

## Workaround

```python
# In _category() and _related(), replace:
(fm.get("metadata", {}).get("hermes", {}) or {})
# with:
((fm.get("metadata") or {}).get("hermes") or {})
```

## Related

- PR #56638 (closed, not merged) covered the malformed-YAML-string variant
- Commit 05cbddc contains the proper fix on `main`

items.title: [Feature]: Add optional privacy filter for MoA reference outputs

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

## Feature request

Please add an optional privacy/redaction filter for Mixture-of-Agents reference outputs before they are displayed, traced, or passed to the aggregator.

In Hermes MoA, each named MoA preset appears as a selectable model under the `moa` provider. When a MoA preset runs, reference models provide analysis first, and the aggregator is the acting model that writes the final assistant response and emits tool calls. Hermes also renders each reference model's output as a labelled block before the aggregator's final answer.  
References:
- https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/mixture-of-agents
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/releases/tag/v2026.7.1

That makes MoA much easier to use, but it also creates privacy risk when reference outputs contain sensitive data before they are:

- shown in the UI
- passed to the aggregator
- saved in MoA traces, such as `moa.save_traces`
- copied into logs, screenshots, or debug dumps
- used in automated workflows, goals, or cron jobs

## Why this matters

The privacy issue is strongest when MoA mixes local/private models with cloud/API models.

Hermes supports local LLMs through OpenAI-compatible local endpoints such as llama.cpp and MLX/omlx. The local-LLM guide describes this as providing full privacy and zero API costs.  
Reference:
- https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/local-llm-on-mac

But in a mixed-provider MoA preset, a local model's reference output may still be sent to a cloud/API aggregator.

Example:

moa:
  default_preset: local_cloud_council
  presets:
    local_cloud_council:
      reference_models:
        - provider: custom
          model: Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf
      aggregator:
        provider: openai-codex
        model: gpt-5.5
      enabled: true

In this setup, the local reference model may see or infer sensitive project details, file paths, names, credentials, logs, or private context. Its reference output is then displayed and passed to the API aggregator unless there is a redaction step.

The reverse is also useful:

moa:
  presets:
    cloud_local_council:
      reference_models:
        - provider: anthropic
          model: claude-opus-4.8
      aggregator:
        provider: custom
        model: Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf
      enabled: true

In that case, cloud/API references could be filtered before being shown, traced, or persisted locally.

## Computer Use privacy concern

This is especially important for Hermes Computer Use.

Hermes Computer Use can interact with desktop apps through clicking, typing, scrolling, dragging, screenshots, and accessibility-tree observations. Those observations may include sensitive information the user did not explicitly type into the prompt.
Reference:

- https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/computer-use

Examples of sensitive computer-use observations include:

- emails and messages
- account pages
- names, addresses, and phone numbers
- browser tabs and URLs
- local file paths
- private project names
- terminal output
- credentials or tokens accidentally visible on screen
- app/window titles
- form fields or document contents
- screenshot-derived text
- accessibility-tree text

In a mixed-provider MoA preset, a local/private reference model may summarize or reason over a computer-use observation, and that reference output may then be shown in the UI, saved in traces, or passed to a cloud/API aggregator.

A privacy filter would reduce accidental leakage from screenshots, accessibility trees, terminal output, documents, browser pages, and other computer-use context.

## What should be filtered

Before reference outputs are displayed, logged, traced, or passed to the aggregator, Hermes could optionally redact sensitive spans such as:

- personal names
- email addresses
- phone numbers
- physical addresses
- private URLs
- private dates
- account numbers
- local file paths
- repository names or private project identifiers
- terminal command output containing secrets
- visible browser tab titles or URLs
- app/window titles
- screenshot-derived text
- API keys, tokens, passwords, and other secrets

## Why this matters

MoA is now a first-class selectable provider/model in Hermes, so users may run MoA as their normal active model rather than as a rare one-shot mode.

This makes it easier to accidentally route sensitive intermediate reasoning across provider boundaries, especially with presets that combine:

- local LLM references with cloud/API aggregators
- cloud/API references with local/private aggregators
- multiple API providers in the same ensemble
- automated MoA runs through goals, cron, gateway sessions, or desktop/TUI sessions

A privacy filter would help preserve the value of local/private models when they are used inside a mixed-provider MoA ensemble.

## Implementation idea

OpenAI recently released OpenAI Privacy Filter, an open-weight model for detecting and redacting PII in text:

- https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-privacy-filter/
- https://github.com/openai/privacy-filter

The OpenAI Privacy Filter repository describes it as a bidirectional token-classification model for PII detection and masking in text, intended for high-throughput data sanitization workflows that can run on-premises. That makes it a relevant possible backend for this feature.

This feature does not need to be tied to OpenAI specifically. Hermes could support a pluggable privacy-filter interface, such as:

- regex-based secrets scanner
- local PII detector
- OpenAI Privacy Filter
- custom command/hook
- future provider-specific redaction backends

## Important distinction

This is not asking for the aggregator to call an extra tool.

This is a MoA pipeline/privacy feature:

reference models
   ↓
privacy filter / redaction layer
   ↓
display / traces / aggregator context
   ↓
aggregator
   ↓
final answer / tool calls

The goal is to reduce sensitive-data exposure before reference outputs are displayed, persisted, or sent across provider boundaries.

### Proposed Solution

## Possible config shape

One possible design:

moa:
  privacy_filter:
    enabled: true
    apply_to:
      - reference_display
      - aggregator_context
      - traces
    mode: redact
    replacement: "[REDACTED]"
    categories:
      pii: true
      secrets: true
      credentials: true
      local_paths: true
      project_identifiers: true
      computer_use_observations: true

Or per preset:

moa:
  presets:
    local_cloud_council:
      reference_models:
        - provider: custom
          model: Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf
      aggregator:
        provider: openai-codex
        model: gpt-5.5
      privacy_filter:
        enabled: true
        apply_to:
          - reference_display
          - aggregator_context
          - traces
      enabled: true

A stricter provider-boundary version could support rules like:

moa:
  privacy_filter:
    enabled: true
    rules:
      - when_source_provider: custom
        when_destination_provider:
          - Nous Portal
          - OpenRouter
          - z.ai / GLM
          - Kimi / Moonshot
          - MiniMax
          - Qwen Cloud
          - Alibaba Cloud
          - Xiaomi MiMo
          - Tencent TokenHub
          - DeepSeek
          - Ollama Cloud
          - Qwen OAuth
          - MiniMax OAuth
          - StepFun
        action: redact

This would let users preserve the privacy value of local models when their outputs cross into cloud/API providers.

### Alternatives Considered

## Alternatives considered

Use only local models

This preserves privacy but loses the quality benefits of MoA with frontier API models.

## Use only cloud/API models

This avoids local-to-cloud leakage, but it removes the privacy and zero-API-cost benefit of local models.

## Manually redact prompts

Manual redaction does not cover reference model outputs, computer-use observations, traces, screenshots, terminal output, or accidental sensitive details generated during intermediate reasoning.

## Disable MoA traces

This helps with persistence, but it does not protect the aggregator context or labelled reference-output display.

## Trust the aggregator provider

This may be acceptable for some users, but it does not address mixed-provider boundaries, local-model privacy expectations, or accidental leakage from Computer Use.

### Feature Type

Configuration option

### Scope

Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

```shell

```

items.title: [Bug] TUI kanban notifications never delivered — poller only watches process completions, not kanban_notify_subs

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary

Kanban task event notifications are never delivered to TUI sessions. The root cause is a delivery-path gap: the TUI notification poller only watches `process_registry.completion_queue`, never polling `kanban_notify_subs` for kanban task events. Meanwhile the gateway's `_kanban_notifier_watcher` correctly reads `kanban_notify_subs` but has no adapter for `tui` platform subscriptions (TUI is not a gateway-channel platform).

The same gap likely affects `api_server` (WebUI) subscriptions.

Related: #59890 documents the symptoms (18 subscriptions, 0 deliveries across tui + api_server).

## Root Cause

Three systems, two delivery paths, neither complete:

### 1. Subscription creation (works correctly)
`tools/kanban_tools.py:974-979` — `_maybe_auto_subscribe()` correctly writes `kanban_notify_subs` rows with `platform="tui"` and `chat_id=<session_key>`. The docstring claims "the TUI notification poller (`tui_gateway/server.py`) reads `kanban_notify_subs`" — but it doesn't.

### 2. Gateway kanban watcher (no delivery to tui/api_server)
`gateway/kanban_watchers.py:115` — `_kanban_notifier_watcher()` reads `kanban_notify_subs`, matches events, and delivers via `self._authorization_adapter(plat, ...)`. For `platform="tui"`, there is no TUI adapter — TUI is not a gateway messaging channel. For `platform="api_server"`, similarly no adapter. The subscription is rewound via `_kanban_rewind` but never delivered.

### 3. TUI notification poller (never reads kanban_notify_subs)
`tui_gateway/server.py:8301` — `_notification_poller_loop()` polls only `process_registry.completion_queue` for background process completions. It was designed for process notifications. Kanban task notifications go through a separate table (`kanban_notify_subs` + `task_events`) that the TUI poller never reads.

## Fix Direction

The TUI notification poller should also poll `kanban_notify_subs` for kanban task events belonging to the session, and emit `status.update` messages when new terminal events are found. This reuses the existing TUI notification infrastructure.

The gateway's `_kanban_notifier_watcher` should skip (not rewind) `tui` and `api_server` platform subscriptions — these are handled by their respective local pollers, not the gateway.

## Related Files

- `tools/kanban_tools.py:974-979` — subscription writes `platform="tui"` with incorrect assumption
- `gateway/kanban_watchers.py:115-336` — gateway notifier with no tui adapter
- `tui_gateway/server.py:8301-8473` — TUI poller only watches process completions
- `gateway/config.py:191` — `API_SERVER` exists in Platform enum but no adapter

items.title: [Bug]: Session title uniqueness is global across sources — invisible TUI sessions block desktop renames

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

Renaming a session in the desktop sidebar fails with "already exists" when the target title is held by TUI sessions that are invisible in the desktop UI. The user sees no conflict but cannot use the name.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a TUI session with a specific title (e.g. `hermes chat` → sessions get auto-titled, or use `hermes sessions rename <id> "Test Title"`)
2. Open the desktop app
3. Right-click any session in the sidebar → Rename
4. Type the same title used by the TUI session
5. Error: the rename is rejected as if the name already exists, but no session with that name appears in the sidebar

## Expected Behavior

Sessions from different sources (TUI vs desktop) should not block each other's titles. The desktop sidebar only shows desktop sessions, so TUI session titles should not collide. Archived sessions should also not block active renames.

## Actual Behavior

The rename fails with an "already exists" error. The conflicting session is invisible because the desktop sidebar filters by `source='desktop'`, but the title uniqueness check is global across all sources.

## Affected Component

- [x] CLI (interactive chat)
- [x] Other — session DB / state.db

## Operating System

macOS 25.5.0 arm64

## Python Version

3.11.15

## Hermes Version

v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream 05cbddc0

## Root Cause Analysis

Two enforcement points in `hermes_cli/session_db.py` apply title uniqueness globally without scoping by source or archived status:

**1. Application-level check (`set_session_title`, line ~120):**
```python
existing = self.db.execute(
    "SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE title = ? AND id != ?",
    (title, session_id),
).fetchone()
```
No `source` filter — checks every session in the database.

**2. Database unique index:**
```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_sessions_title_unique ON sessions(title) WHERE title IS NOT NULL
```
Not scoped by `source` or `archived`. The `WHERE title IS NOT NULL` is the only filter.

The result: TUI sessions block desktop renames (and vice versa), and archived sessions block active renames — even though neither is visible in the respective UI.

The desktop sidebar only displays `source='desktop'` sessions, making the conflict invisible to the user.

## Proposed Fix

**`session_db.py` — scope the application-level check by source:**
```python
existing = self.db.execute(
    "SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE title = ? AND id != ? AND source = ?",
    (title, session_id, self.source),
).fetchone()
```

Optionally also exclude archived sessions:
```python
    AND archived = 0
```

**`session_db.py` — recreate the unique index as source-scoped:**
```sql
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_sessions_title_unique;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_sessions_title_unique ON sessions(source, title) WHERE title IS NOT NULL;
```

Both changes are small and backward-compatible.

items.title: Desktop: option to anchor streamed answers at the top while reading

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Feature Description

Add a Hermes Desktop setting or reading mode that prevents long streamed assistant answers from immediately scrolling the top of the answer out of view.

Current behavior: when an assistant response streams, the thread follows the bottom of the growing response. For long answers, the beginning of the answer quickly moves above the viewport. A user who wants to read from the top has to manually scroll back up to find where the answer started.

Requested behavior: when a new assistant answer starts, the Desktop app should be able to keep the viewport anchored near the start of that assistant response, or otherwise make the start of the response easy to return to, while still allowing an explicit “jump to latest/bottom” action.

## Motivation

Long streamed answers are hard to read in Hermes Desktop because the top of the answer can disappear while the model continues generating. This is especially frustrating when the answer is structured and the important framing is at the beginning.

A user report described the experience as:

> when a answer is provided to a prompt of mine, it doesn't scroll away from my prompt as I keep on having to scroll back to my prompt to be able to read the answer as given from the top. I'm missing the top of all the long answers

## Proposed Solution

Possible UX options:

1. Add a Desktop setting such as **Reading mode for streamed answers** / **Anchor new responses at top**.
2. On `thread.runStart`, scroll to the beginning of the new assistant turn and hold there unless the user chooses to follow the bottom.
3. Keep the existing “follow bottom” behavior as the default if maintainers prefer, but expose a per-user preference.
4. Show a visible “Jump to latest” / “Follow response” button when the viewport is intentionally held above the streaming tail.
5. Alternatively, add a per-response affordance to jump to the start of the current assistant answer.

## Alternatives Considered

- Manually scroll upward once the answer starts. This works only if the user reacts quickly and can still make it awkward to find the exact top of the answer.
- Ask the assistant for shorter/chunked answers. Useful, but this shifts a UI readability problem into prompting style.
- Existing bottom-follow behavior is useful for watching a response finish, but it is not ideal for reading long answers from the start.

## Related

This is related to, but distinct from, #37675. That issue is about long sticky user prompts visually covering assistant output. This request is about streamed assistant responses auto-following the bottom, causing the beginning of long answers to leave the viewport before the user can read them.

## Environment

Observed/reported in Hermes Desktop on macOS.

Local Hermes version checked while filing:

```text
Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1) · upstream 05cbddc0
```

items.title: feat(desktop): URL-based live preview in preview panel (embedded browser for dev servers)
items.body:
## Feature Request: URL-based live preview in Desktop preview panel

### Core Ask

Extend the existing Desktop preview rail (right panel) to accept live URLs, not just local files. This would turn the preview panel into an embedded browser that renders live web applications during development (React/Vite/FastAPI/etc. on localhost).

### Current state

The preview panel already renders Markdown and HTML files from disk. This proves the WebView-based rendering pipeline exists. But it cannot navigate to a live URL like `http://127.0.0.1:8765`.

### Desired behavior

```
Agent: "dev server running at http://127.0.0.1:8765"
User clicks link → preview panel navigates to that URL
→ Real-time rendering of the live web app
→ Supports hot-reload (page stays live as dev server updates files)
→ Navigation controls: back/forward/reload
```

### Why

Claude Code has this feature natively (Claude Preview panel) and it is transformative for frontend development workflows. Users can see UI changes in real-time without switching windows. Hermes already has the underlying WebView capability in the preview panel — this is about plumbing URL navigation into it.

### Technical hints

- The preview panel already uses WebView for HTML rendering
- Needs: URL input or `preview_load_url` tool action + basic navigation controls (back/forward/reload)
- The existing desktop titlebar could add a "URL" action or the `/preview` slash command could accept URLs
- Related to #59838 (wide preview control — makes the panel usable for web previews) and #58854 (clickable links in chat → open in preview)

### Real-world use case

Building a FastAPI+React+pywebview desktop app at `ecomm-detail-app`. Dev server on port 8765. Current workflow:
1. Start server in Hermes terminal
2. Manually open Chrome in separate window
3. Switch back to Hermes for code changes

With URL preview: `terminal` → start server → `/preview http://127.0.0.1:8765` → see app live in Hermes panel → iterate without leaving Hermes.

### Current workaround

Using MCP Chrome DevTools tools (screenshot/snapshot/click/evaluate) to drive external Chrome. Functional but not seamless — requires Chrome debug mode and lacks real-time visual feedback.

items.title: Per-profile empty Nous auth.json dead-ends at runtime before merging shared store (partial fleet outage with provider: nous)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
# Bug report: per-profile empty Nous `auth.json` dead-ends at runtime before merging the shared store **Component:** `hermes_cli/auth.py` — `resolve_nous_runtime_credentials()` (≈ line 5564–5570) **Severity:** partial fleet outage when using `provider: nous` with multiple profiles **Reproduced:** 2026-07-07, Hermes multi-bot deployment (14 profiles + main gateway) --- ## Summary When a Hermes profile's local `auth.json` has `providers.nous.access_token = None` (but the **shared** Nous OAuth store `~/.hermes/shared/nous_auth.json` holds a valid token), the **runtime** credential path raises `AuthError: No access token found for Nous Portal login.` *before* it ever consults the shared store. The bot then replies to every message with: ``` ⚠️ Provider authentication failed. Check the configured credentials; raw provider details are in the gateway logs. ``` The non-runtime resolver `resolve_nous_access_token()` merges the shared store **first** (line 5167) and so succeeds — which is why the bug is invisible to any off-path probe but fatal on the live request path. --- ## Reproduction 1. Deploy ≥ 2 profiles under `~/.hermes/profiles//`. 2. Log in once (populates the shared store). Some profiles end up with a local `auth.json` where `providers.nous.access_token` is `None` (e.g. after a revoked `refresh_token` leaves only a stale `last_auth_error`, or a profile that never completed a local login). 3. Use a model with `provider: nous` (e.g. `tencent/hy3:free`). 4. Send a message to the affected profile. **Observed (journalctl -u hermes-bot@

.service):** ``` WARNING gateway.run: Primary provider auth failed: No access token found for Nous Portal login. — trying fallback ``` **Why only some bots fail:** profiles that already hold a valid local `access_token` pass the check and work; profiles with an empty local token hit the dead-end. This makes the failure look "partial" / mysterious. --- ## Root cause In `resolve_nous_runtime_credentials()` (hermes_cli/auth.py), the `with httpx.Client(...)` block begins: ```python access_token = state.get("access_token") refresh_token = state.get("refresh_token") if not isinstance(access_token, str) or not access_token: raise AuthError("No access token found for Nous Portal login.", provider="nous", relogin_required=True) # ← raises BEFORE merge ``` The shared-store merge `_merge_shared_nous_oauth_state(state)` is only reached *later* (~line 5579), inside `if force_refresh or invoke_jwt_status is not None`. Because `access_token` is `None`, the function raises at line ~5568–5570 and the merge is never attempted. By contrast, `resolve_nous_access_token()` calls `_merge_shared_nous_oauth_state(state)` at line ~5167 *before* reading `access_token`, so it recovers the shared token and succeeds. The two paths disagree on whether the shared store is a fallback. `_merge_shared_nous_oauth_state` (≈ line 4660) copies the shared token in whenever the shared `refresh_token` is non-empty AND (`refresh_changed` OR shared token is fresher). With an empty local `access_token`, `local_access_exp = 0.0 < shared_access_exp`, so the merge would succeed — *if the runtime path reached it*. --- ## Proposed fix Attempt the shared-store merge before raising, mirroring the non-runtime resolver: ```diff --- a/hermes_cli/auth.py +++ b/hermes_cli/auth.py @@ -5564,6 +5564,18 @@ def resolve_nous_runtime_credentials( with httpx.Client(timeout=timeout, headers={"Accept": "application/json"}, verify=verify) as client: access_token = state.get("access_token") refresh_token = state.get("refresh_token") + # Recover a missing local access token from the shared Nous OAuth + # store before giving up. Sibling profiles that logged in populate + # ~/.hermes/shared/nous_auth.json; a profile whose own auth.json has + # access_token=None would otherwise dead-end on every API call and + # never consult the shared store (resolve_nous_access_token() merges + # first and succeeds, so this path must too). + if not isinstance(access_token, str) or not access_token: + with _nous_shared_store_lock(timeout_seconds=max(timeout_seconds + 5.0, AUTH_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)): + if _merge_shared_nous_oauth_state(state): + access_token = state.get("access_token") + refresh_token = state.get("refresh_token") + _persist_state("runtime_shared_merge_on_empty_token") + if not isinstance(access_token, str) or not access_token: raise AuthError("No access token found for Nous Portal login.", provider="nous", relogin_required=True) ``` This fixes the whole bug class (any profile with an empty local token but a valid shared token), not just the one site. `_merge_shared_nous_oauth_state` already requires a non-empty shared `refresh_token` and only overwrites when the shared token is fresher, so the change is safe and idempotent. ### Regression test (suggested) With a temp `HERMES_HOME` whose `auth.json` has `providers.nous.access_token = None` and a shared store `~/.hermes/shared/nous_auth.json` holding a valid token, assert that `resolve_nous_runtime_credentials()` returns the shared token instead of raising `AuthError`. --- ## Workaround (for affected deployments, no code change) For each profile, call the non-runtime resolver once (it performs the merge and writes the shared token into the profile's `auth.json`), then restart the bot: ```bash cd /root/.hermes for p in ; do HERMES_HOME=/root/.hermes/profiles/$p HERMES_PROFILE=$p \ /path/to/venv/bin/python - <<'PY' import sys sys.path.insert(0, '/path/to/hermes-agent') from hermes_cli.auth import resolve_nous_access_token resolve_nous_access_token(timeout_seconds=8) PY done # then: systemctl restart hermes-bot@

.service (external shell) ``` --- ## Environment - Hermes multi-bot deployment: 14 `hermes-bot@.service` + 1 `hermes-gateway.service` - Model: `tencent/hy3:free` / `provider: nous` - Shared store `~/.hermes/shared/nous_auth.json` token valid (verified via direct `curl .../chat/completions` → HTTP 200); auto-refreshes via `refresh_token`. - 6 of 14 profiles had `access_token = None` + stale `last_auth_error` from a revoked refresh session (weeks earlier) → reproduced the dead-end exactly.

items.body:
Image file exists at: `~/.hermes/composer-images/composer_2026-07-07_xxx.png`
But the message has no reference to it.

## Proposed Solution

Store the image file path(s) in the message record:

```json
{
  "role": "user",
  "content": "[The user attached an image: ...]",
  "attachments": [
    {
      "type": "image",
      "path": "C:\\Users\\xxx\\AppData\\Roaming\\Hermes\\composer-images\\composer_2026-07-07_xxx.png",
      "description": "..."
    }
  ]
}


When the model needs to reference the image in follow-up questions, it can use `vision_analyze` to re-load and re-analyze the image from disk.

## Benefits

1. **Zero additional storage cost** — image files are already saved to disk
2. **100% accuracy** — model can always see the original image, not just a lossy text description
3. **Token savings** — don't need to store verbose English descriptions; can re-analyze on demand
4. **Better UX** — users can ask follow-up questions about old images without re-sending them

## Current Workaround

Users must re-send the image when they have follow-up questions. This is inconvenient, especially for:
- Quick screenshots taken during work
- Images from other apps that are no longer available
- Complex diagrams that are hard to re-create

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.0
- Windows 10
- Desktop app (TUI)

items.title: Silent model switch on successful fallback — no user notice on gateways; add fallback activation notification + session metadata

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

When the primary model fails (rate limit / auth / 5xx) and a `fallback_providers` entry takes over, the swap is completely silent from the user's perspective. The docs describe this as intended:

> "Swaps the model, provider, and client in-place […] Continues from exactly where it left off, just using a different model."

The only logging happens when **all** fallbacks are exhausted (`Auxiliary <task>: ... all fallbacks exhausted` at WARNING). A **successful** switch emits nothing — no chat notice, no log line at INFO/WARNING, no gateway message. I verified on v0.18.0 that there is no user-facing notification string for a successful fallback switch anywhere in the agent layer.

## Real-world impact

Yesterday I deliberately selected a specific (more capable, more expensive-tier) model for an important task over the Telegram gateway. Mid-session the provider started returning HTTP 400 (plan limits), Hermes silently swapped to my fallback (a much cheaper model), and the session continued as if nothing happened. I only discovered it afterwards by inspecting `state.db` — the `sessions` row showed `model=<primary>` but `billing_provider=<fallback provider>`.

This is a trust problem: the user believes model X produced the output, while model Y actually did. On CLI/TUI the `runtime_footer` with the `model` field can reveal it (if enabled), but **gateway platforms (Telegram/Discord/etc.) have no equivalent surface at all**, which is exactly where unattended/important sessions tend to run.

For governance-sensitive workflows (model attestation, audit trails, cost control) a silent in-place model substitution is effectively an integrity gap. My only workaround today is `fallback_providers: []`, i.e. giving up failover entirely to guarantee I always know which model is talking.

## Proposed feature

1. **Emit a visible notice on every successful fallback activation** — both:
   - a log line at WARNING (e.g. `Fallback activated: <primary provider/model> → <fallback provider/model> (reason: 429 after N retries)`), and
   - a user-facing message in the session/chat (CLI, TUI, and all gateway platforms), e.g. `⚠ Primary model unavailable (429). Continuing with deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro.`
2. **Config knobs**, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   fallback_notice: chat   # off | log | chat (default: chat)
   ```
   Optionally `fallback_mode: notify | ask | off` — where `ask` pauses and asks the user before switching (valuable for attended sessions; unattended sessions could keep `notify`).
3. **Record the switch in session metadata** — e.g. a `model_switches` field (timestamp, from, to, reason) in the `sessions` table, so `model` vs `billing_provider` is no longer the only forensic trace.
4. Same treatment for **delegation/subagents** inheriting the parent fallback chain — the parent's final report should state which model each subagent actually ran on.

## Why default-on matters

Fallback resets cached prefixes and changes output quality/cost characteristics; both are things users reasonably want to know about at the moment they happen, not days later from a database. A one-line chat notice preserves the "keeps working" spirit of fallback while removing the silent-substitution problem.

## Environment

- hermes-agent v0.18.0 (Windows 11, venv install)
- `fallback_providers` (top-level) with a single entry; primary via subscription OAuth provider
- Reproduced over Telegram gateway; confirmed via `state.db` `sessions` (`model` vs `billing_provider` mismatch)

items.body:
## Context

Follow-up to #60020 / PR #60042 (session title uniqueness scoped per source).

## Problem

Two helper methods in `hermes_state.py` still resolve titles **globally** without a `source` filter:

1. **`resolve_session_by_title` (line 2834)** — used by `hermes -c "My Session"` to resume a session by title. Without a `source` filter, it can return a TUI session when the user expects a desktop session (or vice versa) when cross-source title collisions exist.

2. **`get_next_title_in_lineage` (line 2863)** — generates auto-suffixes like "My Session #2". Without a `source` filter, it counts across all sources, so a TUI session "My Session" causes a desktop session to get "My Session #2" even though "My Session" is free in the desktop namespace.

## Expected behavior

Both methods should scope their queries by `source` (ideally the caller's source, or the active session's source) so that title resolution and auto-suffixing respect the per-source uniqueness boundary established in #60042.

## Affected code

- `hermes_state.py:2834` — `resolve_session_by_title`
- `hermes_state.py:2863` — `get_next_title_in_lineage`

## Notes

This is a separate concern from the rename bug — the rename fix is complete and correct. This issue tracks the UX consistency follow-up so that resume-by-title and auto-titling behave intuitively once cross-source collisions are allowed.

items.title: [Bug]: deepseek-v4-flash model missing from pricing table; cache_read pricing absent for deepseek-chat

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Overview

Two related gaps in the DeepSeek pricing table (`_OFFICIAL_DOCS_PRICING` in `agent/usage_pricing.py`) prevent cost estimation from working correctly for `deepseek-v4-flash` and, more broadly, for any DeepSeek model with prompt caching enabled.

---

### 1. `deepseek-v4-flash` is absent from the pricing table

The model `deepseek-v4-flash` (configured as `model.default` in many `config.yaml` setups and returned by DeepSeek's API) has no entry in the pricing dictionary. The table currently includes:

- `("deepseek", "deepseek-chat")` — the legacy model identifier
- `("deepseek", "deepseek-reasoner")`
- `("deepseek", "deepseek-v4-pro")`

Because the billing route resolves to `("deepseek", "deepseek-v4-flash")`, `_lookup_official_docs_pricing()` returns `None`, and the session cost is reported as `status="unknown"` / `$0.00`.

---

### 2. `deepseek-chat` (and by extension `deepseek-v4-flash`) lacks `cache_read_cost_per_million`

Even the existing `deepseek-chat` entry does not define `cache_read_cost_per_million`. When `estimate_usage_cost()` encounters any `cache_read_tokens` — which is typical for multi-turn conversations where DeepSeek serves prior context from its prompt cache — it reaches this guard on line 878–886:

```python
if usage.cache_read_tokens:
    if entry.cache_read_cost_per_million is None:
        return CostResult(amount_usd=None, status="unknown", ...)
```

The result is that cost remains **perpetually unknown** for any session benefiting from caching, even though DeepSeek's billing pipeline does support discounted cache-hit rates.

It is worth noting that `deepseek-v4-pro` already has this field configured correctly (`cache_read_cost_per_million=Decimal("0.0145")`), suggesting this may simply be an oversight for the flash / chat tier.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `model.default: deepseek-v4-flash` and `provider: deepseek` in `config.yaml`.
2. Start a conversation and exchange several turns so that prompt caching becomes active.
3. Inspect the session cost — it will show `estimated_cost_usd=0.0` with `cost_status="unknown"` regardless of actual API usage.

---

## Expected Behavior

- `deepseek-v4-flash` should resolve to pricing consistent with `deepseek-chat` (they are the same model; only the API identifier differs).
- The cache-read discount should be reflected in cost estimates, following the same pattern already established for `deepseek-v4-pro`.
- According to [DeepSeek's published pricing](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing), cache hits are billed at approximately ¥0.1/1M tokens versus ¥0.5/1M for cache misses (an 80% discount).

---

## Suggested Fix

A few approaches, any of which would resolve this:

1. **Add `deepseek-v4-flash` as a first-class entry** in `_OFFICIAL_DOCS_PRICING` with the same rates as `deepseek-chat`, including a `cache_read_cost_per_million` (e.g., `Decimal("0.014")` following the 10× discount pattern from v4-pro, or the latest published DeepSeek rate).
2. **Introduce model-name normalization** in `_lookup_official_docs_pricing()` — analogous to the existing Anthropic and Bedrock normalization paths — that maps `deepseek-v4-flash` → `deepseek-chat` before lookup.
3. **Backfill `cache_read_cost_per_million` on the `deepseek-chat` entry** as a baseline fix, since the missing field causes `estimate_usage_cost` to bail out early regardless of model resolution.

---

## Environment

| Component | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| Hermes | `main` (commit `05cbddc`) |
| Model | `deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-chat` |
| Provider | DeepSeek (`https://api.deepseek.com`) |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 |
| Python | 3.11 |

---

*Discovered while investigating why cost estimation always returned "unknown" for a production Hermes instance. Happy to provide more detail or test a proposed fix.*

items.title: Desktop GUI: switching profiles loses session — 'Session not found' (404)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Report

### Environment
- **OS**: macOS 26.5.1
- **App**: Hermes Desktop GUI (mac-arm64)
- **Profiles in use**: zhuhuishi, liangyuan, comfyui

### Description

Switching between profiles in the Desktop GUI causes the previous session to be permanently lost. When switching back, the GUI reports **"Session not found" (404)** and the user is forced to start a new conversation, losing all context.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Desktop GUI and start a long conversation under profile **A** (e.g. `zhuhuishi`)
2. Switch to a different profile **B** (e.g. `liangyuan`) via the profile picker
3. Switch back to profile **A**
4. Observe the error in the GUI — the previous session is gone

### Actual Behavior

After switching back, the GUI shows:

```
Error invoking remote method 'hermes:api': Error: 404: {"detail":"Session not found"}
```

The backend logs show the profile backend was reaped and killed via SIGTERM:

```
Starting Hermes backend for profile "liangyuan" via Hermes at ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
Reaping idle profile backend "liangyian" (idle > 600s)
Hermes backend for profile "liangyuan" exited (SIGTERM)
```

The WebSocket connection drops and reconnects, but with only ~8 messages exchanged before disconnecting again (`16:10:27` accepted → `16:10:32` closed, 8 messages). The session data exists in `state.db` but the GUI cannot recover it.

Subsequent attempts result in repeated `API call failed after 3 retries: Connection error.` errors because the backend for the original profile was killed and the new one has no session context.

### Expected Behavior

When switching back to a previously active profile, one of the following should happen:

1. **Preferred**: The GUI reconnects to the existing session seamlessly, restoring the full conversation context
2. **Acceptable**: If the backend was reaped, the GUI should detect this and offer a `/resume` option to restore the session from `state.db`
3. **Minimum**: The GUI should not silently discard the session — it should warn the user that switching profiles will end the current conversation

### Impact

This is a **data-loss bug** for users who work across multiple profiles. Any long conversation context (tool outputs, file edits, decisions) is irretrievably lost when switching profiles.

### Evidence

**`desktop.log`** — Session not found error from renderer:
```
Uncaught (in promise) Error: Error invoking remote method 'hermes:api': Error: 404: {"detail":"Session not found"}
```

**`desktop.log`** — Profile backend lifecycle (repeated pattern):
```
Starting Hermes backend for profile "zhuhuishi"
Starting Hermes backend for profile "liangyuan"
Reaping idle profile backend "liangyuan" (idle > 600s)
Hermes backend for profile "liangyuan" exited (SIGTERM)
Starting Hermes backend for profile "liangyuan"
Reaping idle profile backend "liangyuan" (idle > 600s)
Hermes backend for profile "liangyuan" exited (SIGTERM)
```

**`gui.log`** — WebSocket connection drops during profile switch:
```
16:10:22 ws closed ... messages=8801 detached_sessions=1
16:10:27 ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:53607
16:10:32 ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:53607 messages=8 detached_sessions=0
```
The new WS connection only survived 5 seconds with 8 messages — far too short to re-establish a full session.

### Workaround

Before switching profiles:
1. Use `/save` to manually save the current session
2. Switch profiles
3. After switching back, use `hermes --resume` to restore the saved session

### Suggested Fix

- On profile switch, the desktop process should either keep the backend alive (don't reap active sessions) or gracefully save the session state before sending SIGTERM
- On reconnection, the GUI should attempt to `/resume` the last active session for that profile from `state.db`
- If session recovery fails, the GUI should display the session list and let the user choose which to resume
